records.title: CVE-2026-46300, Linux kernel: local privilege escalation via xfrm ESP-in-TCP ("Fragnesia"), listed by CISA as exploited and chained with the PHP2Shell flaws to reach root, PoC public
records.headline: CVE-2026-46300 (Fragnesia): CISA lists the Linux kernel root flaw as exploited, chained with PHP2Shell
records.summary: CVE-2026-46300 ("Fragnesia", CVSS 7.8) is a local privilege escalation in the Linux kernel's xfrm ESP-in-TCP path, one of three CVEs Red Hat groups as "Dirty Frag"; CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says it can be chained with the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root, and Dream Research reports such a chain against 25 Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall and management servers and a US government-affiliated network. Its public exploit overwrites /usr/bin/su in the page cache, and Red Hat confirms RHEL kernels are affected (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28 · Dream Research, 2026-10-29 · Red Hat RHSB-2026-003).
actions: Patch CVE-2026-46300 on every Linux host that runs PHP or other internet-facing code, then on multi-tenant hosts, container nodes and CI runners: apply the distribution kernel update and reboot; until then, where IPsec is not in use, block and unload the `esp4`, `esp6` and `rxrpc` modules (this breaks IPsec), and drop the page cache so a file already modified in memory reloads from disk.

On any PHP web host, appliance or management server that was reachable and unpatched for the PHP2Shell flaws, look for PHP files in web-reachable directories that nobody deployed, an outbound SSH session from the host that a systemd service or an rc.local entry keeps up, and password-spray bursts against Active Directory from the host's address, because Dream Research reports a chain of the two flaws that did exactly that.

records.title: CVE-2026-115731, Puppet Enterprise before 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 and 2026.0.1: deserialization of a crafted agent report gives code execution as the Puppet service user to any holder of a CA-signed agent certificate, and unauthenticated where the CA autosigns; CISA lists it as exploited (CVSS 4.0 9.4)
records.headline: Puppet Enterprise report-deserialization RCE is on CISA KEV; upgrade to 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 or 2026.0.1
records.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-115731 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-17 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe. A client holding any CA-signed agent certificate can run code on a Puppet Enterprise server as its service user by sending a crafted report, and where the CA autosigns requests without strong verification an unauthenticated attacker can first obtain that certificate; a trigger event has been public since 2026-11-03, and Puppet Enterprise 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 and 2026.0.1 carry the fix. The same advisory fixed CVE-2026-115732, a certificate-name authorization bypass (CVSS 4.0 9.0) that lets a certificate for a name extending a real host name authenticate as that host; CISA lists only CVE-2026-115731.
actions: Upgrade every Puppet Enterprise server to 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 or 2026.0.1 (Puppet Core to 9.1.3 or 8.22.2, OpenVox Agent to 9.3.0 or 8.32.0 and OpenVox Server to 9.2.0 or 8.18.0; open-source Puppet gets no fix) and, until the upgrade is in, stop the CA from autosigning certificate requests without strong verification and audit the certificates it issued for names nobody enrolled or that collide with an existing node name, because CISA lists the deserialization flaw as exploited, any holder of a CA-signed agent certificate reaches code execution on the server and a colliding name authenticates as another host.

records.headline: Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13, 3.3.14 fix seven memory flaws; Veria's Rails exploit not found yet: update the interpreter
records.summary: The Ruby project released 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14 on 2026-11-18 for seven memory-corruption flaws in the regexp engine and in string case conversion, three rated Critical, and says it knows of proofs of concept that reach remote code execution. Veria Labs, which found the case-conversion flaw independently (CVE-2026-132825, a one-byte heap overflow), says Rails and classic-style Sinatra are exposed without authentication in their default configuration and announced a code-execution proof of concept on stock Rails for 25 November 2026, which its page, blog feed and GitHub organisation did not show as released on 2026-11-27; no exploitation is reported. GitHub Enterprise Server and older GitLab branches now carry the fix. Ruby 3.2 and earlier are end of life, and the interpreter itself, not a gem, must be updated.
actions: Update the Ruby interpreter to 4.0.10, 3.4.13 or 3.3.14 on every application host, worker, CI runner and container image that runs Rails, Sinatra or other Ruby code that handles untrusted text, rebuild the images and restart the workers, because updating a gem does not fix the interpreter, Rails is exposed in its default configuration and Veria Labs' Rails exploit, announced for 25 November 2026, may be released at any time.

Upgrade every self-managed GitLab to 19.6.1, 19.5.8 or 19.4.10 or later, or on an older branch to 19.3.10, 19.2.11, 19.1.11, 19.0.12 or 18.11.15 (a self-compiled installation rebuilds Ruby 3.3.14 or 3.4.13 instead), because GitLab ships the Ruby fix as critical patch releases and Veria Labs' Rails exploit is announced.

records.title: CVE-2026-102489 / CVE-2026-102490, Zammad helpdesk: a session-hijack remote code execution and a zammad-to-root escalation, both reported exploited since 21 September; 7.2.2 fixes the root flaw on DEB and RPM installs
records.headline: Zammad 6.5.5 emergency-fixes the exploited session-leak RCE on 6.5; 7.2.3 now supersedes 7.2.2 (root escalation)
records.summary: DIVD, the Dutch vulnerability-disclosure CSIRT, says attackers entered its network on 2026-09-21 through two Zammad flaws it calls previously unknown: CVE-2026-102489, a session hijack leading to code execution as the zammad user in versions 6.3.0 to 6.5.4, and CVE-2026-102490, a local escalation from that user to root. NCSC-NL states both have been exploited since 21 September and CISA listed both in KEV on 2026-10-02; Zammad says the code-execution flaw is exploitable only on 6.5 and older, and Horizon3 published the root cause and a working exploit for it on 2026-10-07. Zammad 7.2.2 (2026-10-08) fixes the root escalation, which affects only DEB and RPM (packager.io) installations, Zammad 7.2.3 of 2026-11-11, a critical security update, supersedes it, and 6.5.5 (2026-10-15) is an emergency fix for the code-execution flaw in the otherwise unsupported 6.5 series; 7.2.1 (2026-10-06) had fixed 27 newly published advisories in 7.2.0 and earlier, two rated critical, none with a CVE id and none reported exploited. DIVD's forensic report of 2026-11-25 says the attacker likely used ARTEX and moved from the Zammad host to Jira and Confluence by ARP poisoning and forged administrator session tokens.
actions: Copy the application and network logs of every self-hosted Zammad instance, then upgrade it to Zammad 7.2.3, the critical security update of 2026-11-11 that supersedes 7.2.2, and add the Remote-User header-clearing line next to X-Forwarded-User in its nginx or Apache2 configuration (the Docker images apply it automatically); a 6.5 instance that cannot be upgraded yet gets the 6.5.5 emergency fix from Zammad's new 6.5 package repository, and an older instance that cannot be upgraded goes offline.

On every instance that was internet-reachable on 6.3.0 to 6.5.4 since 2026-09-21, run DIVD's log-check script, and treat a hit, or any DEB or RPM host where code ran as the zammad account, as compromised, rotating every credential its database held (mail-channel passwords, OAuth client secrets and refresh tokens, API tokens) and revoking cloud OAuth tokens as well as isolating the host, because DIVD's forensic report shows the attacker read those tables and network isolation does not revoke tokens.

records.headline: nginx2root: five unauthenticated flaws reach worker RCE, Rapid7 PoC public; update to 1.31.10, 1.30.8, Plus 37.3.1.1
records.summary: F5 and the nginx project fixed five memory-corruption flaws in the nginx data plane on 2026-11-18, two in HTTP/2 and one each in HTTP/3, the resolver and the mail proxy, which CERT-EU says can lead to unauthenticated code execution with the privileges of the worker process; NCSC-NL scores all five CVSS 4.0 9.2, NCSC.ch and Wiz the two HTTP/2 flaws and Rapid7 CVE-2026-123007. The memory-corruption fixes are in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 and NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1, nginx 1.31.10, 1.30.8 and NGINX Plus 37.3.1.1 and 37.0.9.1 add a fix for one CPU-exhaustion flaw, and NGINX Plus R33 to R36 have no update. Rapid7 published a proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007, CERT-EU reports no exploitation, and NCSC.ch, CERT-EU, CERT.at and NCSC-NL issued warnings; Unit 42 reached pre-authentication code execution through CVE-2026-123633 as the worker user in a lab, on a non-default configuration and with a separate memory leak that F5 has not given a CVE. Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled as affected, Veeam lists its 13.1 Software and Infrastructure Appliances (fixed through Veeam Updater), Cisco, Siemens and Synology list products with fixes pending or none, Fortinet confirms FortiOS, FortiProxy, FortiMail, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer not impacted and still has FortiAuthenticator and dozens of other products under investigation.
actions: Update every internet-facing nginx to 1.31.10 or 1.30.8 (NGINX Plus to 37.3.1.1 or 37.0.9.1) and restart the process, because a reload does not replace the running executable, 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 leave the ssl_early_data CPU-exhaustion flaw open and five unauthenticated flaws reach code execution as the worker with Rapid7's proof of concept for one of them public.

On every Veeam Software Appliance and Infrastructure Appliance 13.1 install the Veeam Updater package now instead of waiting for the automatic Sunday 14:00 install, and limit TCP 443 to trusted networks until then, because Veeam lists both as affected by the two HTTP/2 flaws and HTTP/2 cannot be disabled on them.

Update Synology DSM 7.4 to 7.4.1-90080-2 or above, DSM 7.3 to 7.3.2-86009-6, DSM 7.2.2 to 7.2.2-72806-11, DSM 7.2.1 to 7.2.1-69057-14, DSM 7.1 to 7.1.1-42962-10 and BeeStation OS 1.5 to 1.5.6-68000 (Synology recommends 7.3.2-86009-6 or above on DSM 7.2.x), and on DSM Enterprise 1.0, where the fix is still listed as ongoing, turn HTTP/2 off under Control Panel, Network, Connectivity, because CVE-2026-123007 affects DSM with HTTP/2 enabled.

records.title: ARTEX: Microsoft reports Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, running an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework against hundreds of organizations, with privileged cloud access in under three hours in some cases, and Expel sees the same infrastructure abuse Okta self-service registration
records.headline: FBI: various actors run ARTEX against many sectors, government included; Microsoft now names six users
records.summary: Microsoft reports that since at least September 2026 Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, has used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework, to automate scanning, password spraying and OAuth-application abuse against hundreds of organizations across many industries including government, reaching privileged cloud access in under three hours in several cases; Expel saw the same infrastructure create its own accounts through Okta self-service registration. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report on 2026-10-31 that since late August they have seen ARTEX, PentAGI and CAIRN operated in incident-response cases, with ARTEX adopted by extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters whose victims include US government organizations, and that the original ARTEX repository was taken down in October while forks keep it in circulation. CrowdStrike and Recorded Future document another actor using the framework, and Seoul police referred a criminal group's leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23 for extorting 38 of more than 90 organizations, with the same framework according to BleepingComputer. Microsoft adds on 2026-11-06 another cluster, the Cambodia-based, financially motivated Storm-3358 targeting financial organisations, and Check Point reads ten exposed operator consoles that show near-autonomous, opportunistic ARTEX campaigns. CERT-EU says AI-driven activity against the EU institutions it protects highly likely involved ARTEX. The FBI's FLASH of 2026-11-13 says a variety of actors have used ARTEX since at least August against sectors including financial services, government, technology and defense, and lists the observed techniques, among them cloud-trust and vendor-credential pivots, Kudu abuse and Active Directory credential theft. Microsoft's defender guide of 2026-11-25 widens its named ARTEX users to six, adding the North Korean clusters Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet and the clusters Crystal Typhoon and Salt Typhoon, says ThreatBook now sells an ARTEX Pro, and lists detections on the web server, in identity logs and on egress. Wiz shows that ARTEX and Cairn write a numeric intent ID into names they create in victim environments, ARTEX's drawn from a per-installation counter it does not reset by default, a hunt pivot, and Huntback's exposed console shows a Global Administrator takeover at a South Korean university.
actions: In every Okta org that allows self-service registration, review the accounts created since 2026-10-13 and every Okta Verify enrollment on them, and remove self-created accounts that nobody provisioned.

records.headline: PAN-OS management interfaces rooted via PHP2Shell and a kernel flaw, both exploited per Palo Alto: hotfix, then check
records.summary: Palo Alto Networks' advisory, first published on 2026-10-21 and revised since, says active exploitation has been observed against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet, and Dream Research, with Unit 42's verification, reports a custom PHP2Shell build chained with a Linux kernel flaw that rooted 25 PAN-OS firewall and management servers in the United States, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea and went on to attack a US government-affiliated Active Directory. The advisory lists every release below the hotfix for its train, of PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1, 11.2, 11.1 and 10.2 and of Panorama, as affected through the management web interface by CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS-B 9.2); all twenty hotfixes are released, and GlobalProtect and the captive portal are not affected. Palo Alto's bulletin PAN-SA-2026-0015 of 2026-11-24 says exploitation of that kernel flaw has been observed against internet-exposed management interfaces and lists a later hotfix per train that fixes it. A device that was exposed and unpatched needs a compromise check as well as the hotfix, and CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26.
actions: Take the management interface of every PA-Series and VM-Series firewall and Panorama off the internet now by restricting it to a jump box or trusted internal addresses, because Palo Alto reports active exploitation against internet-exposed management interfaces, and install the hotfix PAN-SA-2026-0015 lists for your maintenance release (12.2.4-h3; 12.1.4-h15, 12.1.7-h15, 12.1.10-h6; 11.2.4-h25, 11.2.7-h25, 11.2.10-h19, 11.2.13-h6, 11.2.16-h3; 11.1.4-h40, 11.1.6-h42, 11.1.7-h14, 11.1.10-h38, 11.1.13-h18, 11.1.16-h6; 10.2.7-h41, 10.2.10-h45, 10.2.13-h29, 10.2.16-h14, 10.2.18-h15), which includes the PHP2Shell fix and fixes the kernel flaw as well.

Rotate the directory bind account, HA replication keys, certificate private keys and device authentication keys of every PAN-OS firewall and Panorama that was reachable from the internet while unpatched and shows a PHP web shell or a tunnel, because the chain Dream Research recovered harvested exactly those from rooted firewalls, and the hotfix does not remove a web shell or tunnel already in place.

records.summary: Mitel's advisory MISA-2026-0012 of 2026-11-16, revised on 2026-11-24 to list the CVE ids, covers five flaws in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of MiCollab 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and earlier, led by an unauthenticated blind command injection scored CVSS 3.1 10.0 (CVE-2026-133323) and an unauthenticated XML injection scored 9.0 that could run commands (CVE-2026-133303). CISA added all five to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 2026-11-25 without naming an actor, victim or technique, while Mitel's own page says nothing on attacks; Accenture APEX Labs reports exploitation before Mitel's 2026-11-16 advisory, with web-shell activity at one victim before 23:00 UTC on 2026-11-15 and root within about 30 minutes, so a server patched now cannot be assumed clean. Mitel offers a patch through its portal (KB000129195) and says restricting external access to the AWV component reduces the risk; the 10.3.0.18 release that Mitel named as the fix for its July advisory is itself in the affected range.
actions: On every MiCollab on 10.3 (10.3.0.18) or earlier whose AWV component was reachable from outside, including through a MiVoice Border Gateway web proxy, take a forensic image first, then apply Mitel's patch KB000129195 (after moving to 10.3.0.18 where needed) and restrict external access to the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing component, then reset the LDAP connector account and any Kerberoastable service accounts and rotate administrator, SIP trunk and file-share credentials, because APEX Labs found exploitation before Mitel's advisory, root within about 30 minutes and directory credentials taken from the LDAP configuration.

records.summary: CVE-2026-99362 is an unauthenticated heap overflow in the Linux kernel NFS server (nfsd) over NFSv4.1 or 4.2, scored CVSS 3.1 9.8 in the CVE record, that OpenSec says it turned into a root shell with one TCP connection to port 2049. It is fixed upstream in 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2 and 7.4-rc1 (later also 5.10.275, 5.15.226, 6.1.193 and 6.6.163), but on 2026-11-27 Ubuntu and RHEL 9 and 10 list no fixed kernel; the exploit is private and no exploitation is reported.
actions: On every Linux host that serves NFS (nfsd loaded, NFSv4.1 or 4.2 on, TCP 2049 listening on a non-loopback address), limit TCP 2049 to the storage network now, where clients do not need NFSv4.1 and 4.2 set vers4.1=n and vers4.2=n in /etc/nfs.conf and restart nfs-server, then install the first kernel your distribution ships for CVE-2026-99362 and reboot, because Ubuntu and RHEL 9 and 10 list no fixed kernel on 2026-11-27 and OpenSec says one unauthenticated connection reaches a root shell.

records.title: SoftwareOK: Q-Dir 12.83 to 12.85 and DesktopOK 12.82 and 12.85 installers from the vendor's official site carried a Python remote-access tool, ASEC says the update function may have been affected too, and reinstalling may not remove it
records.headline: SoftwareOK Q-Dir and DesktopOK installers carried a Python RAT; check hashes, reinstalling may not remove it
records.summary: AhnLab ASEC reports that Q-Dir 12.83.0.0 to 12.85.0.0 and DesktopOK 12.82.0.0 and 12.85.0.0 installers distributed from SoftwareOK's official site were tampered with and install a Python remote-access tool that compares running processes with 1,206 security-product names. ASEC says copies updated through the update function may be affected, has not found how the files were replaced, and the vendor's pages carry no notice as of 2026-11-27.
actions: Inventory every Windows endpoint that installed or updated Q-Dir or DesktopOK since 2026-10-28, compare each installer's SHA-256 with the value on SoftwareOK's download page, and isolate any host with a bundled Python interpreter under ProgramData or a scheduled task that runs one, treating its credentials as stolen, because ASEC says simply uninstalling and reinstalling the program may not remove a Python RAT already installed.

records.title: Java4Shell, CVE-2026-114938, OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later and Oracle Java SE on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI: a heap overflow in the Base64 decoder that Calif chains into pre-authentication code execution in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate; fixed in 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 and 27.0.1.1, GreyNoise reports exploitation attempts, none confirmed successful against its sensors (CVSS 3.1 8.1)
records.headline: Java4Shell: OpenJDK Base64 heap overflow chained to pre-auth RCE in Jira and Keycloak; update Java, attempts seen
records.summary: Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update and the OpenJDK advisory of 2026-11-17 fix CVE-2026-114938, an out-of-bounds write in the AVX-512 Base64 decoder that Calif, one of its two credited reporters, scores CVSS 4.0 9.2 and says it turned into pre-authentication code execution in the default configurations of Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate; Oracle scores it CVSS 3.1 8.1 with high attack complexity. Only x86-64 hosts with AVX-512 VBMI are affected, a trigger proof of concept is public, Calif withholds its product chains, a second researcher claims a working exploit with no release stated, GreyNoise reports exploitation attempts without a confirmed success against its sensors, and VulnCheck says a working exploit is available to its customers. NCSC.ch and BACS warn operators to update internet-reachable Java applications and identity services first, and Cisco's advisory, at version 1.4, lists Catalyst Center, IOS XE and ISE as not affected while Siemens lists Siveillance Control, Siveillance Control Pro and Industrial Edge Management Pro and Virtual with no fix yet.
actions: On every x86-64 host with an AVX-512 VBMI processor that runs Java 17, 21, 25 or 27, update the JDK to 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 or 27.0.1.1 (Oracle builds; Ubuntu and Debian packages carry the same fixes under their own build numbers, other distributions use theirs) or 8u513-perf, then restart the Java processes and rebuild containers, internet-reachable applications and the identity, build and artifact servers Calif names (Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins, PingFederate) first; where that waits, start the JVM with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics, or with -XX:UseAVX=2 on x86-64 hosts only.

records.title: PolinRider: a North Korea-linked loader reaches developers through force-pushed forged commits in at least 7,609 GitHub repositories, hijacked npm releases and a fake employer's take-home test, and reads its server address from an Ethereum wallet
records.headline: PolinRider: forged backdated commits, npm hijacks and a fake recruiter run a loader at build or folder open
records.summary: Apiiro found the PolinRider loader in at least 7,609 GitHub repositories owned by 2,330 accounts, where stolen GitHub access force-pushes a copy of the owner's own commit, with the same author, message and date, plus a loader hidden after hundreds of spaces in a build configuration file. Sonatype found the same loader in 12 hijacked npm releases and JFrog in a fake employer's take-home test and scripted camera check; none relies on an npm install script, the server address is read from an Ethereum wallet, and removing the code does not revoke the access that pushed it. SafeDep later found a Python variant of the loader in 375 public repositories, and StepSecurity traced force-pushed commits that ran in a project's release CI and published 40 infected installers.
actions: Search every branch of your organisation's and suppliers' GitHub repositories for a semicolon followed by 200 or more spaces or tabs in JavaScript, TypeScript and build configuration files, for a utils package or conftest.py that runs node, and for .vscode/tasks.json tasks that run node when a folder opens; on any hit, rotate every GitHub and npm token reachable from the developer machines and CI runners that built the repository and review force-pushes, deploy keys, Actions secrets and releases since the infection, because deleting the loader does not revoke the access that pushed it.

records.title: Claroty Team82: Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration system managers: undocumented 'code-of-the-day' authentication bypass and post-authentication command-injection RCE with thousands of publicly accessible management interfaces
records.headline: Danfoss AK-SM 800A hidden 'code-of-the-day' login is on CISA's exploited list; two post-auth flaws follow
records.summary: Companion disclosure to Claroty's Copeland research, same team and publish day. Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration system managers, used in supermarkets, cold-storage facilities and warehouses, carry an undocumented 'code-of-the-day' authentication bypass (CVE-2025-41450) that Claroty says gives a fully authenticated administrative session and that Danfoss and CISA describe as generating a web report with internal IPs, usernames and store names, a post-authenticated OS command injection in the alarm-email configuration (CVE-2025-41451), and an Nginx configuration-injection flaw enabling denial of service (CVE-2025-41452). Claroty's search of public internet-scan platforms found thousands of exposed management interfaces. CISA added CVE-2025-41450 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 2026-11-25 without naming a campaign.
actions: Upgrade Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration system managers to firmware R4.3.1 (build 4.2 closes CVE-2025-41450 alone) on every deployment, and where that cannot happen immediately take the management interface off the public internet, treating the thousands of internet-exposed devices Claroty found as a priority, because CISA lists CVE-2025-41450 as exploited.

records.title: Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controllers compromised in France, at least six more European countries and Switzerland, with France blaming the IRGC unit Shahid Kaveh for the October campaign; Midnight Blue reports six unpatched pre-authentication flaws in AK-SM 800A firmware up to 5.3.2
records.headline: Danfoss AK-SM 800A: six unpatched pre-auth RCE flaws, Strict mode does not remove them; France blames IRGC
records.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of French stores, and on 2026-11-09 France's foreign ministry attributed that campaign, and only that campaign, to the Iranian unit Shahid Kaveh. More followed: more than 115 stores in at least six more countries and the first German shops on 2026-11-02, altered cold-room settings at three sites of the French blood service through a supplier, and, per SRF on 2026-11-05, a Köniz butcher and three Volg stores in Switzerland. CERT-FR reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, and NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited. On 2026-11-11 Midnight Blue reported six pre-authentication remote-code-execution flaws in all Danfoss AK-SM 800A firmware up to 5.3.2, and on 2026-11-20 Danfoss published CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS 9.3, an unauthenticated stack overflow in AK-SM 8xxA firmware 5.4.0 and earlier, fix only in an announced 5.5.x) and CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS 9.9, default credentials on every legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800, no fix); CCB says updating, new passwords and Strict mode are insufficient, so removing internet exposure comes first, and BACS's statement of 2026-11-10 that updates fix the known flaws predates the report and does not cover the six. CISA added three older AK-SM 800A flaws (CVE-2023-25914, CVE-2023-25915 and CVE-2025-41450) to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue on 2026-11-25 without tying them to this campaign.
actions: Find every Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controller, and any other refrigeration controller with a remote management interface because not every second-wave site's vendor is confirmed, in facilities you own or that a contractor manages for you and take its management interface off the internet now, restoring access only through a secure VPN or protected network (filtering to the contractor's source addresses is an emergency stop-gap, and CERT-FR asks you to check your insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink); an end-of-life unit that gets no fixes needs replacing, because a factory reset leaves it vulnerable and probably compromised again.

On every such controller that was reachable from the internet, check the whole configuration, defrost ranges, alarm thresholds and notification recipients included, against the intended one, verify the actual temperatures and test that alarms reach staff; for a Danfoss unit that may have been taken over, restart it or otherwise factory-reset it, restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network and reconfigure it for service, then update its firmware, set the security level to Strict and replace the default and any weak passwords, which do not close the six unpatched AK-SM 800A flaws that Midnight Blue and CCB report, so the interface stays off the internet; change all credentials where compromise is suspected and check the devices attached to the controllers, as BSI advises; and on every Copeland or Dixell XWEB unit confirm the factory Admin password was changed and give each contractor a named account with an expiry date.

records.title: GeoServer 3.0.2, 2.28.6 and 2.27.7: a five-step chain from an anonymous WFS request to code execution (CVE-2026-129244, CVE-2026-129243, CVE-2026-120705, CVE-2026-129245, CVE-2026-129242) works on a default installation, was disclosed in advisories published on 2026-11-23 and has a public proof of concept and watchTowr reports exploitation attempts, which NCSC Switzerland relays as actively exploited (CVSS 4.0 9.2 for the critical step)
records.headline: GeoServer: unauthenticated code-execution chain has a public PoC and reported probes; update to 3.0.2, 2.28.6, 2.27.7
records.summary: The GeoServer project published a batch of security advisories on 2026-11-23, most for flaws fixed in 3.0.2, 2.28.6 and 2.27.7, and five of them chain an anonymous WFS request to code execution: a path disclosure, a service-security bypass with a prefixed service name, an XML injection, a predictable remember-me key that forges an administrator session (critical, CVSS 4.0 9.2) and a JDBC deserialization. The reporter, who says it works on a default installation, published a full-chain proof of concept the same day; the project announced the fixed releases on 2026-10-19. watchTowr reports exploitation attempts in the form of error-based probes that create and invoke stored queries, and NCSC Switzerland rates the chain actively exploited; watchTowr is the only observer and the sources name different flaws as exploited.
actions: Update every internet-reachable GeoServer to 3.0.2, 2.28.6 or 2.27.7 (2.27 is end of life, so plan the move to a supported line) and, on any instance that ran an older build while reachable, review the stored queries under the data directory's wfs/query folders and the administrator accounts before trusting the host, because a public proof of concept chains the steps from an anonymous request to code execution and watchTowr reports exploitation attempts.

records.title: 1Password: an attacker used an employee's corporate GitHub account to push malicious code to backend services that downloaded administrative data about a subset of customers, and copied private-repository source code and reached the CI/CD system; vaults were not affected
records.headline: 1Password breach via an employee GitHub account exported customer records; vaults not affected
records.summary: 1Password disclosed on 2026-11-25 that an attacker who had gained access to an employee's corporate GitHub account pushed malicious code to backend services, which downloaded administrative data about a subset of customers: names, email addresses, identifiers, public keys, protocol parameters and tokens embedded in some emailed invitation, provisioning and account-recovery links. The attacker also copied private-repository source code and reached the CI/CD system, and 1Password rotated every credential that may have been exposed. 1Password says vault contents, vault keys and recovery keys were not affected and the exposed tokens need an SSO sign-in or an emailed code, which it lengthened; it does not say how the account was compromised or how many customers are affected.

records.title: SEPPmail Secure E-Mail Gateway before 15.1.2: an unauthenticated template injection on the GINA login page can read and take over any GINA account (CVE-2026-130637, vendor score 9.3) and ten more flaws are fixed in the 2026-11-24 patch release; no exploitation or workaround stated
records.headline: SEPPmail 15.1.2 fixes unauthenticated GINA account takeover (9.3) and ten more flaws; update the gateway
records.summary: SEPPmail's patch release 15.1.2 of 2026-11-24 fixes eleven flaws in Secure E-Mail Gateway versions before 15.1.2, led by CVE-2026-130637 (vendor score 9.3): request values reflected on the GINA login page were processed by the template engine, which could let an unauthenticated attacker read attributes of any GINA account and take it over. Two more rows score 9.2 (a security-question recovery session accepted by the password-change workflows, and a hard-coded fallback secret for Large File Transfer attachments) and an unauthenticated request could reset a registered account's password without the security question. SEPPmail names no exploitation and no workaround, and does not say whether the 15.0 branch is affected.

records.title: Okta Threat Intelligence: AI agents register on Auth0 tenants and Okta organizations with disposable addresses from the mail.tm service, whose single rotating mailbox domain makes blocklists very likely stop matching within weeks; ARTEX, Cairn, CyberStrikeAI and pentestcode each picked it at run time
records.headline: Okta: AI agents sign up with mail.tm; its rotating domain will very likely outdate blocklists within weeks
records.summary: Okta Threat Intelligence, with data from the P0 Labs team of Permiso (now part of Okta), reports that since June 2026, and at scale in October and November, AI agents registered accounts with disposable addresses, mostly from the mail.tm family, on Auth0 tenants and Okta organizations that allow public self-service registration. mail.tm exposes one active domain at a time through an account-free API and replaces it periodically, so a blocklist will very likely stop matching within weeks. Okta reads such sign-ups as a likely early sign that agents are tasked against an organization, and says agents often register through the Auth0 Authentication API, which can skip protections applied in Universal Login.

records.title: Splunk Enterprise SVD-2026-1103: two unauthenticated REST API authentication bypasses that accept an empty shared secret (CVE-2026-76536 in the cluster configuration endpoint, CVSS 3.1 9.4; CVE-2026-76535 in RapidDiag task collection, which runs searches as an authenticated user, 9.1) and three more unauthenticated rows at 7.5; fixed in 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12 and 9.4.17, no exploitation reported
records.headline: Splunk Enterprise: unauthenticated REST bypasses accept an empty pass4SymmKey (CVSS 9.4, 9.1); set the key, upgrade
records.summary: Splunk's SVD-2026-1103 of 2026-11-18 fixes 38 flaws in Splunk Enterprise, among them unauthenticated authentication bypasses in the REST API that rest on an empty shared secret: CVE-2026-76536 (CVSS 3.1 9.4, reads and changes clustering configuration on a standalone instance) and CVE-2026-76535 (9.1, runs search queries as an authenticated user), plus three rows at 7.5, two on an empty or factory-default shared key and one that crashes splunkd. Splunk lists fixes in 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12 and 9.4.17 and a workaround of setting a non-empty pass4SymmKey; it does not say an empty secret is the out-of-the-box state, and no source reports exploitation.
actions: Set a strong pass4SymmKey of at least 12 characters in server.conf on every Splunk Enterprise instance below the fixed versions (the [clustering] stanza for CVE-2026-76536 and CVE-2026-131192; Splunk names no stanza for CVE-2026-76535), with the same value on every node that participates in the service, restart it, remove the RapidDiag app where it is not needed and upgrade to 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12 or 9.4.17, instances whose management API is reachable from user or internet networks first, because the unauthenticated REST bypasses accept an empty shared secret.

records.title: CVE-2026-61500, Rejetto HFS < 3.2.1: predictable session-signing PRNG lets an unauthenticated attacker forge admin sessions to RCE (CVSS 9.3)
records.headline: Rejetto HFS pre-auth session forgery reaches code execution and is exploited since 2026-10-02; update to 3.2.1
records.summary: Rejetto HFS (HTTP File Server) 3.0.0–3.2.0 derives its session-cookie signing key from JavaScript's Math.random() and leaks that generator's outputs to unauthenticated clients, letting an attacker forge an administrator session and reach RCE via the server_code feature (CVE-2026-61500, CVSS 9.3). Fixed in 3.2.1 (2026-07-13). GreyNoise reports an actor exploited it from 2026-10-02 to take over an unpatched HFS server and keep it as a relay in an intrusion campaign, so any exposed instance on an older build needs the upgrade and a compromise check.
actions: Upgrade every internet-exposed Rejetto HFS to 3.2.1 and, on any instance that ran an older build while reachable, look for an SSH key in /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, HFS command hooks and server_code content nobody added, treating a hit as a compromised host, because an actor exploited CVE-2026-61500 from 2026-10-02 and kept a hijacked HFS server as a relay.

records.title: OptimJack: poisoned scripts served by Optimizely, Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly route iPhones to exploit-kit stages, the Optimizely files also carry a crypto clipper and card skimmer, and the University of Basel site loaded a poisoned StorifyMe widget on 2026-11-14
records.headline: OptimJack: Optimizely names the exploited signup-flow flaw; Report URI counts 178 organisations, Zscaler 450+ domains
records.summary: Optimizely says an unauthorized party exploited a flaw in its Web Experimentation account signup flow to impersonate users and add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects, fewer than 5% of its customers, and Report URI counts 178 organisations that served the code on 2026-11-16 while Zscaler ThreatLabz counts more than 450 domains; the Optimizely files carry a crypto clipper and card skimmer and were all clean again by 23:11 UTC that day. Ohey reports that scripts served by Kissmetrics and StorifyMe gained a loader from 2026-11-13 that routes iPhones to the Coruna and DarkSword exploit-kit stages and that minute-ly's loader was replaced outright; Hudson Rock names 21 web properties, among them the University of Basel's StorifyMe widget, and calls the iPhone stages delivery observations, not confirmed compromises. How the Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly files were altered is unknown.
actions: List every page of your organisation's sites, and of the agencies that build them, that has loaded Optimizely project JavaScript since 2026-11-16, or Kissmetrics i.js, a StorifyMe widget or the minute-ly loader since 2026-11-13, capture the bytes the browser receives and compare them with the provider's own project content (a search for the loader's host name misses the variant that hides it in base64), and where a file carries the injected loader remove it, keep the response bytes as evidence and treat the payment, login and form pages that loaded an affected Optimizely file as exposed to card and session theft.

If your organisation or an agency building its sites has an Optimizely Web Experimentation account, audit every Project JavaScript field for code nobody wrote and rotate the API tokens, session tokens and integration keys tied to it, because the attacker impersonated users on targeted accounts to edit that field.

For every page that loaded an Optimizely snippet on 2026-11-16, review the card and cryptocurrency transactions made on it during Optimizely's exposure window (07:51 to 22:24 UTC; Report URI saw the first injection at 04:21 UTC) and keep the web server, CDN, WAF and payment logs that cover the day, because Optimizely says the script was meant to take card details typed into a site's own forms and cryptocurrency transfers.

last_development.summary: Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis of the exploited Directory Service bypass, and a Metasploit module for it is in an open public pull request. Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0011 fixes a second Directory Service bypass, CVE-2026-123903, in vCenter 9.1.2 and 9.0.2.0300, so a 9.x vCenter on 9.1.1.0200 or 9.0.2.0200 needs a further update.

records.title: CVE-2026-123890, VMware vCenter Server: an unauthenticated authentication bypass in the Directory Service gives an administrator session; GTIG reports the suspected China-nexus actor ARMORY CASTLE exploited it from early September, Broadcom lists no workaround; first fixed in 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200 and 9.1.1.0200, with 9.1.2 and 9.0.2.0300 now superseding the 9.x builds (CVSS 3.1 9.8)
records.headline: vCenter auth bypass exploited since September; Metasploit module in public review: patch to 9.1.2, 9.0.2.0300 or 8.0 U3m
records.summary: Broadcom's advisory VMSA-2026-0009 of 2026-11-19 fixes CVE-2026-123890, an authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service of vCenter that needs only network access to vCenter (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with no workaround and, in Broadcom's words, an emergency change. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant say ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus actor, exploited it from early September 2026 to move from a compromised remote-support appliance to vCenter, forge administrator SAML sessions and extract domain-controller data from guest virtual disks on ESXi; Broadcom's advisory does not state exploitation. Fixed builds for this flaw are 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200, 9.1.1.0200 and VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.5, but a second Directory Service bypass fixed on 2026-11-24 leaves 9.1.1.0200 and 9.0.2.0200 affected (9.1.2, 9.0.2.0300 and 8.0 U3m cover both). Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis and a Metasploit module is in a public pull request; vCenter 7.0 has no public fix.
actions: Update every vCenter Server to 9.1.2, 9.0.2.0300 or 8.0 U3m (VMware Cloud Foundation 5.x to 5.2.5 through KB88287), which fix this flaw and, per Broadcom's response matrix, the second Directory Service bypass of 2026-11-24 (some release notes list different CVEs), now as an emergency change, and until it is in, drop inbound TCP 2012 to vCenter from every address that is not an allowlisted management host, as Google's hardening guidance lists, after testing because TCP 2012 is the vCenter SSO control-interface RPC, because GTIG reports exploitation since early September and Broadcom lists no workaround.

On every vCenter that was reachable from an internal host before the update, list the SSO and local administrators on vsphere.local that nobody created, review the SSO signing material and ESXi authorized_keys files, because the actor extracted the SAML signing key and created accounts, which updating does not undo.

records.title: VMSA-2026-0011, VMware vCenter and ESX: a second Directory Service authentication bypass in vCenter (CVE-2026-123903) and two I/O filter service flaws in ESX that give code execution from network access (CVE-2026-123910, CVE-2026-123911), all CVSS 3.1 9.8; no workaround for vCenter, fixed in vCenter 9.1.2, 9.0.2.0300 and 8.0 U3m, no exploitation reported
records.headline: Broadcom VMSA-2026-0011: second vCenter auth bypass and ESX I/O filter RCE, all 9.8; the earlier fix does not cover 9.x
records.summary: Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0011 of 2026-11-24 fixes 23 flaws, among them CVE-2026-123903, a second authentication bypass in vCenter's Directory Service that needs only network access (CVSS 3.1 9.8, no workaround), and CVE-2026-123910 and CVE-2026-123911, I/O filter service flaws in ESX that give code execution from network access (9.8 each). vCenter 9.1.2, 9.0.2.0300 and 8.0 U3m fix the vCenter flaw, so a 9.x vCenter already on the build that fixed the exploited CVE-2026-123890 (9.1.1.0200 or 9.0.2.0200) is still affected; no source reports exploitation of these 23 flaws.
actions: Update every ESX host to ESXi-9.1.2.0-25946735, ESXi-9.0.2.0200-25953133 or ESXi80U3m-25926933 and, on ESX 8.x hosts that must wait, restrict TCP 9080 on the host firewall to the vCenter Server address as KB463535 describes, because CVE-2026-123910 and CVE-2026-123911 give code execution from network access and the restriction resolves only a small portion of the advisory's issues.

records.title: Unit 42: more than ten campaigns in July to September 2026 ran autonomous AI agents from web-shell footholds on vulnerable web applications, with a command-gap median of 1.4 seconds, ===[Title]=== script headers and 40 to 100 unique Base64 payloads per session
records.headline: Unit 42: AI agents behind web shells in 10+ campaigns; hunt 1.4 s command gaps and ===[Title]=== headers
records.summary: Unit 42 tracked more than ten campaigns between July and September 2026 in which different attackers pointed autonomous AI agents at targets in sectors including government, logistics, manufacturing and education. Every campaign began with a web shell on a vulnerable web application, after which the agent did reconnaissance, credential harvesting, privilege escalation and lateral movement mostly with single-use scripts and no compiled implants. Unit 42 reports no new technique but measurable traces: a median gap of 1.4 seconds between commands in a subset of attacks (23.9 seconds in the human phase), section headers such as ===[Title]=== in every campaign, and 40 to 100 unique Base64 payloads per session.

records.title: BACS: first confirmed cyberattacks carried out with AI agents against Swiss companies and critical-infrastructure operators, every known case ending in a compromise; internet-reachable agents such as ARTEX and CyberStrikeAI have almost doubled since October
records.headline: BACS confirms first AI-agent attacks in Switzerland, all successful; critical updates within 24 hours
records.summary: Switzerland's Federal Office for Cyber Security (BACS) said on 2026-11-24 that it has for the first time received reports of attacks on Swiss companies and critical-infrastructure operators in at least two sectors that were carried out with the support of an AI agent, and that in every case known to it the agent led to a successful compromise of the victim's IT systems. It names no framework, case count, sector or entry point for the Swiss cases, says the number of internet-reachable agents such as ARTEX and CyberStrikeAI has almost doubled since October 2026, and recommends critical updates on internet-reachable systems within 24 hours.

records.title: GreyNoise GT13: an unattributed actor that GreyNoise believes used LLM tooling held persistent access to at least 24 Check Point Security Management servers at 22 organisations, government among them, using CVE-2026-16232 and a Rejetto HFS relay hijacked through CVE-2026-61500
records.headline: GT13 holds Check Point management servers at 22 organisations; patching does not evict it, check audit logs
records.summary: GreyNoise reports that an actor it tracks as GT13 had persistent access to at least 24 Check Point Security Management servers at 22 organisations in 17 named countries and territories (Switzerland is not among them), government among seven sectors, with confirmed activity from 2026-10-17 to 2026-11-02. The actor used a script for the SmartConsole authentication bypass CVE-2026-16232, which Check Point confirms and which has been fixed since July, to launch more than 100 management tasks that copied the firewall database and the internal certificate authority. GreyNoise does not know how the actor first got in or who it is, and expects the campaign to be ongoing.
actions: On every Check Point Security Management and Multi-Domain Security Management server, confirm the Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator is installed (R82.10 from Take 36, R82 from Take 118, R81.20 from Take 158), limit Trusted Clients to named administrator addresses, then search the Audit Logs View for "Authentication method: Password based application token" and for any unrecognised administrator name or source address; on a hit, treat the server as compromised, check /etc/ld.so.preload and unfamiliar SSH private keys and treat the firewall database, the internal CA and stored credentials as stolen, because GreyNoise saw the actor copy them from multiple servers and a patch does not evict that access.

records.title: Project Zero: clearing one COFF header flag makes .NET Framework 4 load an untrusted assembly past Windows code-integrity checks (CVE-2026-108398, fixed 2026-10-13); the same behaviour defeated VirtualBox's Windows process hardening (CVE-2026-87268) and is expected to remain a protected-process bypass
records.headline: Project Zero: one-bit change loads untrusted .NET assemblies past UMCI; fixed in October, PPL bypass expected to remain
records.summary: Google Project Zero's James Forshaw shows that .NET Framework 4 falls back to a flat, non-image mapping when an assembly's executable-image header flag is cleared, so protection code that expects to check the loaded image section never sees the load, and that the code-integrity policy check meant to stop the fallback passes on Windows 11 S Mode, letting an untrusted assembly run under User Mode Code Integrity. Microsoft fixed it as CVE-2026-108398 in October 2026 (Important, CVSS 3.1 8.8, publicly disclosed, not exploited); the same behaviour bypassed VirtualBox's Windows process hardening (CVE-2026-87268) and gives code execution as a protected process light, which Microsoft's servicing criteria treat as out of scope.

records.title: Symantec: 41 likely AI-authored PowerShell modules ran under an IIS web shell at an African stock exchange for just over three minutes, hunting secrets in SYSVOL, shared folders, SharePoint, SCCM and TFS, testing them against financial APIs and returning the output as hex-encoded DNS lookups to a public out-of-band testing service
records.headline: Symantec: 41 AI-authored PowerShell modules ran under an IIS web shell and exfiltrated through DNS lookups
records.summary: Symantec's Threat Hunter Team found a toolkit on a stock-exchange web server in an African country in which 41 PowerShell modules ran under an IIS web shell for 3 minutes 12 seconds on 2026-09-20, hunting secrets in Group Policy Preferences, shared folders, SharePoint, SCCM and TFS, testing a guessed password, a reused token and API keys against the exchange's investment API and a securities-depository gateway, and returning their output as hex-encoded DNS lookups to a public out-of-band testing service. Symantec assesses AI authorship from the uniform scaffolding, attributes six older implants on the same server to Witchetty with high confidence but does not attribute the toolkit, and does not know whether any credential worked.

records.title: F5 BIG-IP: six unauthenticated stack overflows rated CVSS 9.8 (CVE-2026-123637, CVE-2026-116953, CVE-2026-120285, CVE-2026-120292, CVE-2026-120722, CVE-2026-121805) crash TMM and may allow code execution where an iRule command or APM policy is configured; fixed only by engineering hotfixes, no exploitation reported
records.headline: F5 BIG-IP: six unauth CVSS 9.8 TMM overflows, fixed only by engineering hotfixes; check iRule and APM use
records.summary: F5's 2026-11-18 notification includes six BIG-IP flaws that an unauthenticated remote attacker can use to terminate the Traffic Management Microkernel and that F5 says may allow remote code execution, each CVSS 3.1 9.8 and each needing a specific virtual-server configuration: one of five iRule commands, or an APM per-request policy that includes both the Client Information and Endpoint Security agents. BIG-IP 21.1, 17.5 and 17.1 are affected, no scheduled release carries the fix and F5 lists no workaround, so the fix is an engineering hotfix from F5; none of F5's advisories says the flaws are exploited.
actions: On every BIG-IP, list the virtual servers whose iRules call GENERICMESSAGE::route, PSC::ip_address, MR::message route, DNS::scrape or PEM::subscriber and the APM per-request policies that include both the Client Information and Endpoint Security agents, internet-facing ones first, and apply the matching engineering hotfix on each such system on 21.1, 17.5 or 17.1 (a system on a custom engineering hotfix needs a new one from F5 support), because F5 lists no workaround and no scheduled release carries the fix.

records.title: CVE-2026-134624, N-able Mail Assure and SpamExperts before 20261121.1943: a server-side request forgery in the LDAP-sync connection check, disclosed after a breach of N-able's hosted cloud, is listed by CISA as exploited (CVSS 4.0 9.3)
records.headline: N-able Mail Assure SSRF CVE-2026-134624 is on CISA KEV after a hosted-cloud breach; revoked tokens need reissuing
records.summary: N-able confirmed on 2026-11-18 that an unauthorized party had reached a web server of its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud, the email-filtering service it runs for managed service providers, and on 2026-11-22 published CVE-2026-134624, a server-side request forgery in the LDAP-synchronisation connection check (CVSS 4.0 9.3, authenticated API user) that build 20261121.1943 fixes; CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-23. N-able says exploitation was confined to one N-able-hosted server, has not said whether the flaw was the way in, and revoked customers' API and OAuth tokens, so integrations need new credentials.
actions: If you buy Mail Assure or SpamExperts through an MSP or hoster, ask the provider whether N-able's partner notice reached it and have it re-create the API and OAuth integrations N-able revoked; on every customer-hosted SpamExperts Local Cloud, confirm the build is 20261121.1943 or later, because CISA lists CVE-2026-134624 as exploited and N-able's incident statements describe only the Hosted Cloud.

records.title: Azure API Management Classic: a flaw let an unknown actor take secrets, named values and tokens from APIM instances; Norway's NSM names Equinor and Skagerak Energi among those hit and tells every APIM user to treat secrets as exposed and rotate them after Microsoft's 2026-11-19 mitigation
records.headline: Azure APIM Classic secrets exposed and exploited; NSM: assume compromise, rotate every token and secret
records.summary: Norway's NSM said on 2026-11-20 that an unknown actor actively went after access tokens, secrets and named values in Azure API Management, that the flaw hit several Norwegian organisations including Equinor and Skagerak Energi, and that it also affects other sectors and countries. Microsoft, in a customer notice quoted by SecurityWeek, identified the issue on 2026-11-18 and closed the access path on 2026-11-19, and says Classic instances were exposed before it identified the issue while v2 tiers are not affected. NSM tells every APIM user to assume secrets and named values are exposed and to rotate all tokens and secrets.
actions: On every Azure API Management instance, read the gateway RuntimeVersion as NSM describes (0.52.x is patched from build 31936, 0.53.x from build 31938, and v2 or Consumption-tier patterns are not affected) and, whatever the result, rotate every named value, backend credential, identity-provider client secret, subscription key and token the instance held, plus the Key Vault secrets it references, then review the Activity, gateway, Key Vault and service-principal sign-in logs for use of the old values, because NSM says to assume secrets and named values are exposed and Microsoft's notice says Classic instances were exposed before Microsoft identified the issue on 2026-11-18 and mitigated it on 2026-11-19.

records.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health: an API flaw present from 2026-07-23 was exploited to read tenant metadata including administrator and technical-contact email addresses; Microsoft fixed it server-side on 2026-11-19 and warns of targeted phishing
records.headline: Entra Connect Health API flaw exploited: admin email addresses read; Microsoft warns of targeted phishing
records.summary: Microsoft told Entra tenants from 2026-11-20 that a flaw in the Entra Connect Health API, introduced on 2026-07-23 and found on 2026-11-09, was exploited for unauthorized read-only access to tenant metadata: administrator and technical-contact email addresses, tenant identifiers and domain names, licence tier and directory-synchronisation status. It fixed the flaw server-side on 2026-11-19, says no customer update is needed and no configuration change was found, and advises expecting targeted phishing against the exposed addresses; it has not said who exploited the flaw, how many tenants are affected or when exploitation began.
actions: Open Azure Service Health in every Entra tenant you run and look for Microsoft's 2026-11-20 security notification; where it is present, warn the administrators and technical contacts whose addresses were exposed to expect targeted phishing and social engineering, because Microsoft says the exposed addresses and tenant details can be used for targeted attacks.

records.title: BabidiGhost: a jailbroken Hermes-based AI agent run against more than 50 targets, mostly in Belgium, France and Switzerland, exported an insurer's customer database and 13 municipalities' archives through public flaws and exposures; MFA, IP allow-listing and server-side validation stopped it
records.headline: BabidiGhost AI agent targeted 50+ organisations, mostly in Belgium, France, Switzerland; MFA and allow-lists held
records.summary: SOCRadar reconstructs a nine-day operation (2026-11-06 to 2026-11-14) in which a low-skill French-speaking operator ran a jailbroken Hermes-based AI agent against more than 50 organisations and datasets, mostly in Belgium, France and Switzerland, breaching two of 14 analysed in depth and partly breaching three, the largest thefts being an insurer's customer database through an unpatched Metabase (CVE-2023-38646) and the archives of more than 13 municipalities through a weak password on a shared IT provider's storage interface, while TOTP, IP allow-listing and server-side validation stopped it. ZATAZ reports that the BlackHatSect0r handle now rents the agent and offers a bank-phishing platform that covers 28 Swiss banks; neither source names a Swiss victim.

records.title: Operation ShadowCloud: Kaspersky's GitDoor and GraphDoor backdoors hide command and control in GitHub, Microsoft Graph with SharePoint, and Ably against government networks in Asia and Africa, delivered through an abused MeshCentral agent and DLL sideloading
records.headline: Kaspersky: ShadowCloud's GitDoor and GraphDoor hide C2 in GitHub and Microsoft Graph, planted via a MeshCentral agent
records.summary: Kaspersky GReAT describes Operation ShadowCloud, an intrusion set identified in early 2026 that abuses the legitimate MeshCentral agent to drop two new backdoors, GitDoor and GraphDoor, with victims in Asia and Africa primarily in the government sector; the entry point is unknown. The operators sideload a loader DLL into a legitimate program beside an encrypted config.ini, and the backdoors take commands through the GitHub API (GitDoor) or Microsoft Graph and SharePoint (GraphDoor), with Ably as a further channel. Kaspersky does not attribute the activity and reports overlaps with FamousSparrow and CopperTurtle; Sophos tracks a fragment as BRONZE SANDCASTLE.

records.title: CVE-2026-125396, Ghostscript before 10.08.0 (Upload2Shell): a font-loader use-after-free breaks the -dSAFER sandbox, and pwn.ai reaches it from an anonymous print job, a viewed Roundcube attachment and public WordPress upload forms; fixed since 2026-09-08, no exploitation reported (CVSS 4.0 8.5)
records.headline: Ghostscript CVE-2026-125396: print jobs, Roundcube attachments and upload forms reach the sandbox escape; update
records.summary: Artifex fixed CVE-2026-125396 in Ghostscript 10.08.0 on 2026-09-08: a crafted PostScript or PDF document turns a use-after-free in the font loader into code execution outside the -dSAFER sandbox, scored CVSS 4.0 8.5 with a local vector. pwn.ai's writeup of 2026-11-21 shows that applications hand untrusted files to Ghostscript indirectly, and it reaches command execution from an anonymous print job to a shared CUPS queue, an emailed attachment viewed in Roundcube and public WordPress upload forms; no source reports exploitation, and only a partial proof of concept is public. Debian and Ubuntu ship fixed packages, and a host update does not reach a copy of Ghostscript bundled in a container image or application.
actions: Update Ghostscript to 10.08.0 or a distribution build that carries the CVE-2026-125396 fix (Debian 12 10.0.0~dfsg-11+deb12u9, Debian 13 10.05.1~dfsg-1+deb13u2, Ubuntu per USN-8949-1) on every Roundcube mail server, CUPS print server and web server with public upload forms, and rebuild the container images that bundle their own copy, because pwn.ai reached the sandbox escape from an anonymous print job, a viewed email attachment and public upload forms, and a host package update does not reach a bundled copy.

records.title: GL.iNet GoodCloud: an exploited cloud remote-management flaw installed malware on routers and Comet KVMs; the cloud fix does not clean infected devices, the vendor's firmware is the clean-up, and RemoteToHome finds that clean-up partial
records.headline: GL.iNet GoodCloud exploited: the cloud fix leaves routers and KVMs infected; install the model's security firmware
records.summary: GL.iNet says an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote-management services (GoodCloud, per BleepingComputer), identified on 2026-11-20, to install malicious software on some GL.iNet routers and KVM devices; the cloud fix stops new infections but, in the vendor's words, does not remove malware from devices already infected. The vendor lists security firmware per model that it says removes the identified malware without a factory reset, while RemoteToHome, which manages many of these routers, reports the clean-up is partial and advises a reinstall with settings discarded for any device that shows a sign. GL.iNet has not said how the flaw worked or how many devices are affected, and a compromised KVM may extend to the computer it controls.
actions: Inventory every GL.iNet router and Comet KVM your organisation or its remote and branch users run, check each for signs of compromise and capture its process list, connections and firewall rules before the firmware upgrade restarts it, then install the security firmware for its exact model, because GL.iNet confirms exploitation, its cloud fix does not clean devices that are already infected and RemoteToHome says an upgrade of an infected KVM removes the evidence.

records.title: Huntress on timeroasting: the unauthenticated MS-SNTP sweep that harvests crackable MACs for computer and trust accounts leaves no logon event, Defender for Identity raised no alert in its tests, modern Windows sends an extended authenticator Huntress now has a cracker for, and the signal that holds is a host asking a domain controller to sign for an account other than its own
records.headline: Timeroasting leaves no logon event; Huntress shows the signal that holds is a host requesting another account's RID
records.summary: Huntress reverse-engineered the MS-SNTP signing code on a patched Windows Server 2025 domain controller and reports that timeroasting, an unauthenticated UDP/123 request that makes a domain controller return a password-derived MAC for any computer or trust account, produces no authentication event for the targeted accounts and raised no Defender for Identity alert across eleven test runs. Modern Windows clients send a 120-byte extended authenticator that public tools could not crack; Huntress published a reference cracker and a hashcat module for it. Packet size is not a usable signal: the check that holds is a source host requesting a RID other than its own computer account, with volume as the fallback.

records.title: CVE-2026-120382, Synology DSM OAuth API: an argument injection lets an unauthenticated remote attacker read or write arbitrary files on the NAS (CVSS 3.1 9.8); fixed in DSM 7.4.1-90080-2 and 7.3.2-86009-6, with DSM 7.2.x, 7.1 and BeeStation OS still unfixed
records.headline: Synology DSM OAuth API flaw lets anyone read or write NAS files; update to 7.4.1-90080-2 or 7.3.2-86009-6
records.summary: Synology's advisory Synology-SA-26:21 (2026-11-19, revised 2026-11-20) fixes CVE-2026-120382, an argument-injection flaw in the OAuth API of DiskStation Manager that lets remote attackers read or write arbitrary files and cause denial of service, scored CVSS 3.1 9.8 with no privileges or user interaction required. DSM 7.4 and 7.3 are fixed in 7.4.1-90080-2 and 7.3.2-86009-6; DSM 7.2.2, 7.2.1, 7.1 and BeeStation OS 1.5 have no fix yet, and Synology's mitigation is to deactivate the OAuth Service package. No source reports exploitation.
actions: Update every DSM 7.4 NAS to 7.4.1-90080-2 and every DSM 7.3 NAS to 7.3.2-86009-6, and on DSM 7.2.x, 7.1 and BeeStation OS, which have no fix, deactivate the OAuth Service package or, for 7.2.x, move to 7.3.2-86009-6 as Synology recommends, because CVE-2026-120382 lets an unauthenticated attacker read or write arbitrary files on the NAS.

last_update.summary: GTIG reports in-the-wild exploitation under CVE-2026-40217 but describes it as a key-regeneration user-ID rebind, not the vendor's guardrail sandbox escape; no source reconciles the two. VulnCheck scores CVE-2026-47101 at CVSS 4.0 8.7.

last_development.summary: CISA added the LiteLLM guardrail sandbox escape CVE-2026-40217, the last step of Obsidian Security's chain, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-18; LiteLLM's own advisory now supplies the description, the proxy-admin prerequisite, the CVSS 4.0 5.9 score and the endpoint block.

records.title: Obsidian Security: a three-CVE chain turns any LiteLLM user into root on the AI gateway; CISA lists the guardrail sandbox escape CVE-2026-40217 as exploited
records.headline: LiteLLM: CISA lists the guardrail sandbox escape CVE-2026-40217 as exploited; the chain gives root on the AI gateway
records.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-40217, the custom-code guardrail sandbox escape in LiteLLM that Obsidian Security chained with CVE-2026-47101 and CVE-2026-47102 into root on the AI gateway, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-18 and describes the exploitation no further; Google's threat-intelligence group attributes an exploited LiteLLM flaw to the same id but describes it as a key-regeneration user-ID rebind, not the sandbox escape. LiteLLM says the flaw needs a proxy-admin credential by default, which the chain's privilege escalation supplies, fixes the chain in v1.83.14-stable and gives a reverse-proxy block for the endpoint.
actions: Pin LiteLLM to v1.83.14-stable or later on every instance and, until it is in, block POST /guardrails/test_custom_code at the reverse proxy or API gateway; on any instance an untrusted user could reach on an older build, rotate every provider API key, the database credentials, any MCP tokens stored in the proxy and the master and salt keys, and audit every Custom Code Guardrail, the litellm_settings.callbacks entries and every proxy_admin holder, because CISA lists CVE-2026-40217 as exploited and the chain reaches those secrets.

last_update.summary: Symantec does not say the side-loaded DLLs are unsigned, and it notes that one of the executable and DLL pairings is used by several threat actors, so the pairing alone identifies neither the malware nor the actor.

records.title: Symantec: a September 2026 intrusion at a US retailer shows attackers switching to AI-generated PowerShell and, about ten minutes after first querying SolarWinds Orion, using the RabbitMQ Erlang cookie bundled with it to run a command on a second server
records.headline: Symantec: AI-assisted retailer intrusion pivots through SolarWinds Orion's bundled RabbitMQ Erlang cookie
records.summary: Symantec reports that after hand-typed commands against a US retailer's web server were blocked, the attackers switched overnight to long, error-free PowerShell scripts and, about ten minutes after first querying SolarWinds Orion, read the Erlang cookie of the RabbitMQ broker bundled with it and ran Orion's own erl.exe to execute a command on a second web server. Symantec assesses AI assistance with high confidence and says no technique was new: the AI supplied speed, while the chain ran through SQL Server command execution, web shells, side-loaded security-vendor executables and domain credential theft.

last_update.summary: Two of the release's CVEs close gaps in the fix for CVE-2026-109619, the PHP2Shell flaw CISA has listed as exploited since 2026-10-26; no exploitation of this release's own CVEs is reported.

records.title: PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36: CVE-2026-129289 lets an unauthenticated request smuggle a second FastCGI request into PHP-FPM and run PHP code when the front end reuses FastCGI connections; the release also fixes the session flaw left open in October and follow-ups to an incomplete earlier fix (CVSS 4.0 9.2)
records.headline: PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36: FPM request smuggling to code execution; the open session flaw is fixed
records.summary: The PHP project released 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and 8.6.0 on 2026-11-19 with fixes for up to 18 CVEs per branch. The most direct is CVE-2026-129289: PHP-FPM keeps unread php://input bytes on a persistent FastCGI connection, so an unauthenticated multipart request can plant a second FastCGI request and run PHP code as the worker, but only behind a front end that reuses FastCGI connections, which standard nginx and Apache setups do not. The release also fixes CVE-2026-115560, left open in October, and follow-ups to the incomplete fix for the exploited PHP2Shell flaw CVE-2026-109619; no source reports exploitation of this release's CVEs or a public proof of concept.
actions: On every PHP-FPM server behind nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on or HAProxy in FastCGI mode, switch FastCGI backend connection reuse off until the server runs 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 or 8.5.13, because CVE-2026-129289 gives an unauthenticated request code execution as the worker wherever a connection is reused and an application path leaves php://input unread.

last_update.summary: FortiClient is exposed to CVE-2026-121529 only where the FortiPAM service is installed, and uninstalling that service is Fortinet's workaround.

last_development.summary: Fortinet revised the FortiOS HA advisory for CVE-2026-126259 on 2026-11-16: FortiGate HA clusters running FGCP, in active-passive and active-active mode, are also affected on the vulnerable builds, though exploitation needs an attack vector adjacent to the HA segment. The advisory adds an HA hardening configuration for fixed builds whose HA segment is not fully trusted; the fixed builds are unchanged.

records.title: Fortinet coordinated security hardening release: the advisories published on 2026-11-10 carry unauthenticated FortiMail, FortiAnalyzer, FortiManager, FortiOS and FortiAuthenticator flaws rated CVSS up to 9.8; FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager 8.0 have no fixed build for the JSON API flaw, FortiOS 7.0 and FortiMail 7.2 are left out of the October fixes
records.headline: Fortinet advisories: FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager 8.0 have no fix for a 9.8 JSON API flaw; FortiMail RCE rows too
records.summary: Fortinet's hardening releases of 2026-10-21 (FortiMail, FortiAuthenticator) and 2026-10-22 (FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer) fixed critical and high-severity flaws, and the advisories withheld until Patch Tuesday were published on 2026-11-10 with critical rows in FortiMail (unauthenticated code execution, SQL injection and IBE account takeover, CVSS up to 9.8), FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager (an unauthenticated JSON API flaw at 9.8, oftp port flaws, FGFM code execution), FortiOS, FortiAuthenticator and FortiClient. The October builds fix most rows, but FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager 8.0.0 through 8.0.2 have no fixed build for CVE-2026-126170 until the upcoming 8.0.3 (workaround: set rpc-permit none), and FortiOS 7.0, FortiMail 7.2 and FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager 7.0 are left to migrate or wait; none of the 2026-11-10 advisories states exploitation.
actions: Upgrade every FortiMail to 8.0.2, 7.6.7 or 7.4.9 (a 7.2 unit moves to a fixed release; 7.2.10 for CVE-2026-126150 is not released), every FortiAuthenticator to 8.0.4 or 6.6.11, every FortiOS to 8.0.2, 7.6.8, 7.4.13 or 7.2.14 (a 7.0 unit migrates), and every FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer on 8.0.0 or 8.0.1, 7.6, 7.4 or 7.2 to 8.0.2, 7.6.8, 7.4.12 or 7.2.13 (7.0 migrates), internet-facing units and FortiMail first, because the advisories describe unauthenticated code execution and account takeover and Fortinet warns that patch differences show attackers where the weakness sits; keep the FGFM and oftp ports and every administrative interface off untrusted networks.

On every FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager (Cloud variants included) on 8.0.0 through 8.0.2, set rpc-permit none on every administrator profile that has the JSON API enabled until Fortinet releases 8.0.3, because no 8.0 build fixes the unauthenticated 9.8 flaw CVE-2026-126170 and 8.0.2 is affected.

records.title: BundID: automated mass login attempts against Germany's federal citizen accounts lock accounts; the BSI confirms the attack, password sign-in was switched off on 16 November and returned that afternoon behind an e-mail security code, and no compromise is evidenced
records.headline: BundID: mass automated logins lock citizen accounts; BSI confirms; password sign-in now needs an e-mail code
records.summary: On 2026-11-16 Germany's BSI confirmed automated, mass login attempts against BundID, the federal citizen account for online administrative services: failed attempts locked accounts and triggered password-reset mails, and the federal government switched off username-and-password sign-in that morning, then restored it the same afternoon with a mandatory security code by e-mail at every password sign-in, while eID and Elster sign-in stayed open. The BSI has no indication that any account was compromised; Handelsblatt, citing government circles, calls it credential stuffing.
