records.title: N-able N-central: 33 alleged flaws published, and Hotfix 3 (build 2026.4.1.39, 2026-11-16) now fixes 17 more CVE ids and blocks the Legacy API permanently, which 4EverAble2Shell (Apache Axis CVE-2026-90436, exploited on at least 21 servers) and Agent2Shell need; N-able does not say either chain is fixed, and public proof-of-concept code exists for the 17
records.headline: N-central: Hotfix 3 fixes 17 more CVEs and blocks the Legacy API; 4EverAble2Shell exploited; upgrade Agents too
records.summary: An independent researcher published proof-of-concept code on 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-09 for what Huntress counts as 33 critical flaws in N-able's N-central appliance, and a second disclosure on 2026-11-12 added 4EverAble2Shell, a chain through Apache Axis (CVE-2026-90436) that works against Hotfix 2 when the Legacy API is on and is exploited on at least 21 production servers, and Agent2Shell, SYSTEM commands on managed Windows endpoints. Hotfix 2 (build 2026.4.1.26, 2026-11-10) fixed seven CVE ids and Hotfix 3 (build 2026.4.1.39, 2026-11-16) fixes 17 more, hardens how Agents and Probes authenticate and blocks the Legacy API permanently, but N-able does not name either chain or say it is fixed; Huntress reports public proof-of-concept code for all 17 and no exploitation of them in its partners' environments. Every on-premises server and every Agent and Probe must be on Hotfix 3, including those already on Hotfix 2.
actions: Upgrade every on-premises N-central server to 2026.4 Hotfix 3 (build 2026.4.1.39) and every Agent and Probe to 2026.4.1 HF3 even if already on Hotfix 2, confirm the Legacy API is disabled and not reachable from the internet, and on any server that had the Legacy API on check the web logs for POST requests to the Axis endpoint /dms/services/ServerUI carrying a SOAP fault and the host for a symlink at the N-central flag file path, treating a hit as a full compromise, because public proof-of-concept code exists for all 17 new CVE ids, Hotfix 2 did not stop 4EverAble2Shell and N-able does not say Hotfix 3 fixes it.

last_update.summary: Huntress does not tie its 20 August rogue-client incidents to CVE-2026-84869; the exploitation of the flaw it confirms runs from October 2026. The worm-like spread runs from an infected client to every Host that joins a session with it, not the other way round.

last_development.summary: Huntress confirmed exploitation of CVE-2026-84869 against MSP technicians: on 2026-11-12 a guest-pushed batch file ran on a technician's client with no prompt and installed a rogue ScreenConnect client within about nine seconds, while attacker guests were making 688,000 run-file requests on 42 MSP servers between 2026-10-20 and 2026-11-16. Updating the server does not fix it; every technician host client must be on 26.6.5 or later.

records.title: CVE-2026-84869, ConnectWise ScreenConnect: a missing file-transfer authorization check lets an active remote session push and auto-run files on the Host (CVSS 9.9); Huntress confirms exploitation against MSP technicians since October 2026
records.headline: ScreenConnect clients before 26.6.5 run guest-pushed files unprompted; Huntress confirms exploitation against MSPs
records.summary: CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9) lets file-transfer actions inside an already-active ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote session run without the authorization or Host-confirmation step the product is meant to require; ConnectWise fixed it in 26.6.5 on 8 September. Huntress has confirmed exploitation against MSP technicians since October 2026, with attacker guests spraying run-file requests across 42 MSP servers. Earlier, from 20 August, Huntress saw rogue ScreenConnect clients that push their infection chain as an auto-run file transfer on every new connection, behaviour that matches the flaw, though Huntress does not tie those incidents to the CVE.
actions: Update every ScreenConnect technician host client and Access agent to 26.6.5 or later now, not only the server, because the vulnerable code runs on the technician's machine; where that waits, remove the TransferFiles permission from every role and session group (Administration > Security > Roles).

Treat any pre-26.6.5 client that shows a second, unfamiliar RMM tool or an unexplained ScreenConnect connection ID as compromised and reimage it rather than patching in place, because every Host that joined a session with an infected client can have received and run the same infection chain.

On every ScreenConnect server, read a copy of App_Data\\Session.db for guest-originated RanFiles or SentFiles events that overlap an open host connection, and on any hit isolate the technician's workstation and rotate every credential reachable from it (RMM, PSA, vault, customer admin accounts), because Huntress saw one workstation fully compromised nine seconds after its client ran a guest-pushed file.

last_update.summary: Three of the release's unauthenticated 9.8 rows, in Communications Diameter Signaling Router, Communications Unified Assurance and PeopleSoft PeopleTools, are the Brotli flaw CVE-2026-111497, which CISA has listed as exploited since 2026-10-27; those products move to the front of the patch order. Oracle flags no row, and no exploitation of the other rows is reported.

records.title: Oracle's November 2026 Critical Security Patch Update: 56 of its 62 rows at CVSS 9.0 or above are reachable over the network without authentication, six of them at CVSS 10.0 in Access Manager, WebLogic Server, Platform Security for Java and Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition; Oracle flags no row as exploited, but CISA lists the Brotli flaw behind three of them
records.headline: Oracle CSPU: 56 unauthenticated rows at CVSS 9.0+, six at 10.0 in Access Manager, WebLogic, BI; Brotli rows on KEV
records.summary: Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update of 2026-11-17 carries 655 patches, and its risk matrices mark 56 of the 62 rows scoring CVSS 3.1 9.0 or above as remotely exploitable without authentication. Six are CVSS 10.0 with changed scope, in Oracle Access Manager (three rows), WebLogic Server TopLink Integration, Platform Security for Java and Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition, and WebLogic Server and E-Business Suite carry further unauthenticated rows at 9.8. The only exploited flaw among them is the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497, which CISA has listed as exploited since 2026-10-27 and which fills three of the unauthenticated rows; for attacks that need no privileges Oracle's interim measure is blocking the network protocols an attack needs.
actions: Apply the November 2026 CSPU first to Communications Diameter Signaling Router, Communications Unified Assurance and PeopleSoft PeopleTools, whose Brotli rows are the KEV-listed CVE-2026-111497, then block T3 and IIOP to every WebLogic Server from networks that untrusted hosts can reach and patch internet-reachable Access Manager, WebLogic Server, E-Business Suite and APEX or REST Data Services instances, because Oracle marks 56 rows at CVSS 9.0 or above as exploitable without authentication and names blocking the required network protocols as its interim measure for attacks that need no privileges.

records.title: CVE-2026-111497, Brotli decoder flaw in Siemens industrial and software products (Desigo CC, SIMATIC WinCC, Industrial Edge, Teamcenter and Opcenter among them), Mitel MiVoice Business and OpenScape, with Cisco listing Duo Network Gateway, RoomOS and Nexus 3000 and 9000 switches (Guest Shell) in its combined advisory: Desigo CC takes the .NET updates, while most Siemens products, most Mitel updates and the Industrial Edge Common Configurator fix are still pending
records.headline: Brotli flaw: Apple fixes iOS, macOS; Siemens WinCC, UMC, Teamcenter, Opcenter mostly unfixed; Mitel, Cisco listed
records.summary: Between 2026-10-27 and 2026-11-18 Siemens, Mitel and Cisco listed affected products in advisories that cover the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497: Siemens names Desigo CC V8 and V9 (remedy: the latest .NET security updates), Gridscale X DSA V5.3 and Gridscale X PSS®E below V36.8.0 (fixed in V5.4 and V36.8.0), Industrial Edge, where Common Configurator has no fix, and, in two interim advisories of 2026-11-10, 15 industrial products including SIMATIC WinCC V7/V8, WinCC Unified, the User Management Component and TIA Administrator and 28 software products including Teamcenter and the Opcenter family, nearly all with no fix; Mitel names MiVoice Business, six OpenScape products, MiCollab Advanced Messaging and Performance Analytics, with OpenScape SBC fixed in V11R3.4.5 and most other updates planned; Cisco's combined advisory lists Duo Network Gateway (3.4.2), RoomOS and, at version 1.13 of 2026-11-13, Nexus 3000 and 9000 switches running Guest Shell among its products with fixes, a longer list of which is dated up to 2027, without saying which of its CVEs each fix addresses. Cisco says it is not aware of malicious use against any Cisco product, and CISA lists the flaw as exploited. Apple fixed the flaw on 2026-11-09 in iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 and 26.7.3, macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1, Tahoe 26.7.3 and Sequoia 15.8.3, watchOS 27.2.1 and visionOS 27.2.1, and in HomeView Software 27.2 on 2026-11-12 and tvOS 27.2.1 on 2026-11-13.
actions: Install the latest .NET security updates through Windows Update on every Siemens Desigo CC V8 and V9, SENTRON Powermanager V8 and V9 and Integrated PA Suite Tester host, update Siemens Gridscale X DSA V5.3 to V5.4 and Gridscale X PSS®E to V36.8.0, and update WinCC OA V3.20 to V3.20 P17.1 and BRAUMAT and SISTAR to V8.2 Update 5.

On the SSA-242944 products Siemens lists with no fix or no planned fix (SIMATIC WinCC V7/V8, WinCC Unified, WinCC OA V3.21, WinCC Runtime Professional, WinCC Companion, the Profiling Tool, User Management Component, TIA Administrator, COMOS Walkinside and the Project Server Web Administration Tool), disable Brotli compression and decompression at the application or proxy layer where it is not required and add the IIS request-filtering rule that denies br in the Content-Encoding header on UMC (on TIA Administrator when UMC authentication is enabled), and on every Industrial Edge Management instance running Common Configurator uninstall all Management Applications and put it behind a firewall or WAF.

Update OpenScape SBC to V11R3.4.5 and apply Mitel's MiCollab Advanced Messaging patch (KB000129143), and on OpenScape SESAP and Contact Center systems apply the workaround articles KB000129034 and KB000129114, because Mitel has released no update for those two.

records.title: Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI, versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 published on 2026-11-17, carried a credential stealer that a .pth startup hook runs every time Python starts, collecting environment secrets and requesting Azure managed-identity, Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions OIDC tokens; both versions were removed and 1.26.0 is the last clean release
records.headline: Microsoft's agent-framework on PyPI carried a Python-startup stealer in 1.26.1 and 1.26.2; hash-lock the tree at 1.26.0
records.summary: Socket and SafeDep report that versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's official agent-framework metapackage were published to PyPI on 2026-11-17, about 33 minutes apart, with a .pth file that runs a credential stealer whenever Python starts, so a pip install in a CI job is enough. It collects environment secrets and credential files and requests Azure managed-identity, Azure DevOps and, in 1.26.2, GitHub Actions OIDC tokens. Both versions were removed from PyPI and 1.26.0 is the last clean release; a second maintainer account created on the day of the attack can still publish agent-framework and five sibling projects, four of which 1.26.0 installs, and how it got access is not known.
actions: Search lockfiles, requirements files and CI install logs for agent-framework 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 installed since 2026-11-17 20:35 UTC, and on every host or job that ran Python after installing either, treat the environment variables, local credential files, Azure managed-identity and Azure DevOps tokens and, for 1.26.2, GitHub Actions OIDC tokens as stolen and rotate them, then lock the whole dependency tree with hashes at agent-framework 1.26.0 and hold new releases of agent-framework-openai, -purview, -redis, -tools and -postgres, because the maintainer account created on the day of the attack can still publish those siblings and 1.26.0 accepts any release of four of them below 2.0.

records.title: RIKEN Fugaku and Rikyu supercomputers: an intruder entered the internal operational network through the internet-facing operating-status dashboard, planted malicious programs on internal servers and took users' stored SSH private keys and access keys, then tried them on other systems
records.headline: RIKEN Fugaku: intruder entered via the public status dashboard, exfiltrated 430 SSH private keys, tried some elsewhere
records.summary: RIKEN says that between 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-13 an external party used the publicly accessible web page showing Fugaku's operating status to enter its internal operational network, tampered with internal servers (some with malicious programs) and collected and exfiltrated credentials users had stored for other systems: RIKEN's second notice of 2026-11-20 counts 430 SSH private keys, 233 of them without a passphrase. Up to 4,222 Fugaku and 375 Rikyu users are affected, RIKEN confirmed that some of the stolen credentials were tried against other systems, and it suspended Fugaku on 2026-11-14. How the dashboard was breached is still under investigation, and RIKEN names no actor.

last_update.summary: Cisco gives two separate causes for CVE-2026-76466: persistent cookies, and client certificates that go unvalidated when TLS Verify Mode is enabled for clustering; it does not say clustering is what uses the cookies.

last_development.summary: CISA listed CVE-2026-76466 as exploited on 2026-11-20, and F6 reports that soon after a public proof of concept appeared attackers compromised two internet-reachable Expressway X15.5.3 devices, then two internal cluster nodes, with root used for scanning and credential theft; Cisco's advisory still says it knows of no malicious use. Priority moves to high.

records.title: CVE-2026-76466, Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E: unauthenticated root command execution on clustered devices, listed as exploited by CISA and used in an intrusion F6 investigated, fixed in X15.5.20 with no workaround (CVSS 9.8), alongside same-day hardening releases for Unified CM, Unity Connection and Snort 3
records.headline: Cisco Expressway root RCE is exploited (CISA KEV, F6 incident): upgrade clustered units to X15.5.20 and check them
records.summary: Cisco's disclosure of 2026-10-21 fixes CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 3.1 9.8), which lets an unauthenticated attacker who holds persistent cookies run operating-system commands as root on Expressway-C and Expressway-E configured in a cluster; X15.5.3 and earlier get X15.5.20, X14 and earlier must migrate, and there is no workaround. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20, and F6 reports that, soon after a public proof of concept appeared, attackers compromised two internet-reachable X15.5.3 devices, reached two internal cluster nodes through one and ran Python scripts for scanning and credential theft, while Cisco's advisory still says it knows of no malicious use. The same-day hardening releases for the Unified CM family and Unity Connection (up to 9.8, fixed in 15SU5) and for Snort 3 (9.0) are not known to be exploited.
actions: Upgrade every clustered Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E to X15.5.20 now (X14 and earlier has no fix and must migrate) and, until it is in, limit TCP 4371 to 4372 to the cluster peers' addresses as F6 advises, because CISA lists CVE-2026-76466 as exploited and F6 saw two internet-reachable nodes compromised soon after a public proof of concept appeared.

On every clustered Expressway that was reachable before the upgrade, search erlang.log for a nodeup record naming wombat@127.0.0.1 and check for scanning, SMB, SQL Server and WinRM traffic that starts on the Expressway or its cluster peers, treating a hit as a root compromise, because an upgrade does not evict an attacker who already holds root.

records.title: CVE-2026-133968, MONAI Label through 0.8.5: an unauthenticated path traversal in the datastore upload endpoints gives arbitrary file write and code execution, exploited since September 2026 (Amazon says Cairn AI agents found it as a zero-day against East Asian university servers); fixed in 0.8.6, authentication is off by default (CVSS 3.1 9.8)
records.headline: MONAI Label CVE-2026-133968 exploited since September: upgrade to 0.8.6; authentication is off by default
records.summary: The MONAI Label 0.8.6 security release of 2026-11-22 fixes CVE-2026-133968, a path traversal in the PUT /datastore/image and PUT /datastore/label endpoints of the medical-imaging annotation server that writes files anywhere the server process can write, reachable without credentials in the default configuration; the CVE record says it was exploited from September 2026. Amazon Threat Intelligence reports that a Chinese-nexus operator's Cairn AI agents found it as a zero-day, went from API mapping to arbitrary file write in about 11 minutes and later to a root shell on a university server.
actions: Upgrade every MONAI Label server to 0.8.6 (pip install -U monailabel==0.8.6, or the projectmonai/monailabel:0.8.6 image), because CVE-2026-133968 is exploited and every version through 0.8.5 is affected.

On every MONAI Label 0.8.5 or older server that was reachable from an untrusted network, review it for unexpected file changes before it returns to service, starting with sitecustomize.py, authorized_keys and cron entries that the service account wrote and nobody deployed, because the upgrade does not evict an attacker who is already in.

records.title: Canton Basel-Landschaft: attackers took about 97,000 records from a database of work permits for cross-border commuters (permit G) in the cyberattack on the cantonal administration; the canton cannot say which records, assumes all, and names no entry point or actor
records.headline: Basel-Landschaft: attackers took about 97,000 cross-border work-permit records; no entry point or actor named
records.summary: On 2026-11-20 the canton of Basel-Landschaft said that forensic analysis by external experts confirmed the attackers reached a database of work permits for cross-border commuters (permit G) and took data from it: about 97,000 records from applications lodged through its online platform since 2016-11-28, with names, addresses, birth dates, civil status, occupation, the ZEMIS identification number and employers' contact details. The canton cannot say which records left and assumes all did; it names no entry point, tool or actor, took the platform off the network and filed a criminal complaint against unknown persons.

records.title: Cleared Windows event logs are not empty: Arctic Wolf shows that clearing an EVTX log truncates it after the first 64 KB cluster and leaves the earlier records in that chunk's free space, where standard forensic tools do not parse or flag them, and recovered a ransomware encryptor's command line this way
records.headline: Arctic Wolf: a cleared Windows event log keeps earlier records in its first EVTX chunk; carve it
records.summary: Arctic Wolf incident responders report that clearing a Windows event log truncates the EVTX file after the first 64 KB cluster and resets the record numbers, but the first chunk keeps its earlier records in its free space. On a domain controller the System log held 104 allocated events after the final clear, yet the encryptor's full command line, stamped about three hours before the clear, sat inside the allocated file, and Event Viewer, EvtxECmd and Magnet AXIOM showed none of it; a PowerShell log in a second case held 44 records of which one was allocated.

records.title: Webworm's NtMonitor: Rapid7 finds a custom rebuild of the SoftEther VPN Bridge that removes the open-source tool's detection fingerprints (rebranded metadata, renamed handshake endpoints, a custom handshake watermark, an embedded resource archive and an encrypted configuration), attributed with moderate confidence to the China-aligned actor that targets European governments
records.headline: Rapid7: Webworm hides SoftEther VPN Bridge behind NtMonitor branding, new endpoints and an encrypted config
records.summary: Rapid7 describes NtMonitor, a Windows build of SoftEther VPN Bridge 4.44 that it attributes with moderate confidence to Webworm, the China-aligned actor that ESET documented moving to European government targets in May 2026. The rebuild keeps SoftEther's function of bridging a remote network into the victim's LAN and strips its fingerprints: branding, handshake paths, the handshake watermark, the separate resource archive and the plain-text configuration are all changed, and Rapid7 found no backdoor or other added capability. Only one antivirus vendor detected the sample on VirusTotal although it has been public since January.

records.title: Hokkaido: resident-register, support-needed and tax data of the cities of Rumoi and Iwamizawa and the town of Shintoku sat on a subcontractor's development PC infected with the K2F information stealer, which GIS Hokkaido links to the NIKKE game launcher; Rumoi's data was still there after its contract ended
records.headline: Hokkaido: municipal data on a subcontractor's PC hit by K2F stealer via a game launcher; Rumoi's contract had ended
records.summary: On 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-19 the Hokkaido municipalities Iwamizawa, Rumoi and Shintoku disclosed that data they gave their contractor GIS Hokkaido was stored on a development terminal of its subcontractor Rimgate that the K2F information stealer infected overnight on 2 to 3 November: up to 71,002 resident-register and 4,503 support-needed records for Rumoi, whose personal data was still on the terminal after its contract ended, 6,001 resident-register and 986 evacuation-support records for Shintoku, and fixed-asset-tax land and building data for Iwamizawa. GIS Hokkaido told ITmedia that the PC launcher of the game NIKKE is involved and would not say whether Rimgate staff ran the game on the work PC; no leak or misuse is confirmed, and none of the data contains the national My Number.

records.title: CVE-2025-42884, SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal EP-BASIS and EP-RUNTIME 7.50: a JNDI injection that an unauthenticated attacker can use to read or change server information, fixed by SAP Security Note 3660969 in November 2025 and listed by CISA as exploited on 2026-11-20 (CVSS 3.1 6.5)
records.headline: SAP Enterprise Portal JNDI injection from November 2025 is now on CISA KEV; confirm Security Note 3660969 is applied
records.summary: CISA added CVE-2025-42884 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe. The flaw lets an unauthenticated attacker inject JNDI environment properties or a URL used in a JNDI lookup in SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal (EP-BASIS and EP-RUNTIME 7.50) and read or modify server information; SAP rated it Medium, CVSS 3.1 6.5, and fixed it with Security Note 3660969 on its November 2025 Patch Day. No source names an actor, a victim or how it is chained.
actions: On every SAP NetWeaver AS Java with Enterprise Portal (EP-BASIS or EP-RUNTIME 7.50), confirm that SAP Security Note 3660969 is implemented and apply it where it is not, internet-reachable portals first, because CISA lists CVE-2025-42884 as exploited a year after the fix.

records.title: CVE-2026-129448, Apache Roller 4.0.0 to 6.1.5: an unauthenticated request to the XML-RPC endpoint deserializes attacker-controlled objects before authentication and runs code on the server; Apache says it is being exploited, CISA lists it, fixed in 6.1.6 (CVSS 3.1 9.8)
records.headline: Apache Roller XML-RPC deserialization RCE is exploited and on CISA KEV; upgrade to 6.1.6 or later
records.summary: Apache's announcement of 2026-11-17 assigns CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 3.1 9.8) to Apache Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4, the same flaw it disclosed as CVE-2026-82384 for 6.1.5 in September: the XML-RPC endpoint deserializes vendor extension types before authenticating the requester, which gives an unauthenticated attacker code execution. Apache states the flaw is being actively exploited and CISA listed it on 2026-11-20, while neither describes the attacks; Roller 6.1.6 or later fixes it, and switching XML-RPC off in the administration interface does not help on older releases.
actions: Upgrade every Apache Roller to 6.1.6 or later (6.1.7 is the project's best available release) and, where that waits, set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml or remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping and restart; treat any internet-reachable instance on an older release as possibly compromised, because Apache and CISA report exploitation and the request is deserialized before authentication.

records.headline: USI Lugano: forms system exploited 9 to 17 November; mainly contact data, 8,000+ warning e-mails sent
records.summary: The Swiss university USI said on 2026-11-19 (communiqué translated from Italian) that unauthorised third parties had access to data on one of its applications between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-17 by exploiting a vulnerability in the software of an online-forms system that collects job applications, scholarship requests and surveys. Its chief operating officer said on 2026-11-20 that the stolen data are mainly names, e-mail addresses and phone numbers, with a small share of job applications and scholarship requests, that more than 8,000 e-mails warned those concerned, and that AI agents found and exploited the flaw, which is USI's own assessment with no technical evidence given. records.title: Mitel OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager, MISA-2026-0013: two unauthenticated flaws in the Platform component rated CVSS 3.1 10.0 (improper authentication, command injection) and an adjacent-network command injection (9.6); CVE ids pending, fixed in V11 R2.14, Security Mode restricted access is the workaround, no exploitation stated
records.headline: Mitel OpenScape 4000: two unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 Platform flaws; upgrade to V11 R2.14 or restrict access
records.summary: Mitel's advisory MISA-2026-0013 of 2026-11-18 covers three flaws in the Platform component of OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager: an unauthenticated improper-authentication flaw and an unauthenticated command injection, both CVSS 3.1 10.0, and a command injection reachable from the adjacent network (9.6). CVE ids have been requested but not assigned; the fix is V11 R2.14, PLT HF5 on V11 R1.26 or a patch for V10 R0.28 to V11 R0.22, and enabling Security Mode restricted access is Mitel's workaround. The advisory says nothing about exploitation, and it is the second critical Mitel advisory in a week.
actions: Upgrade every OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager to V11 R2.14, apply PLT HF5 on V11 R1.26 or Mitel's patch on V10 R0.28 to V11 R0.22, and until then enable Security Mode restricted access as Mitel's workaround article KB000129263 describes, because two unauthenticated Platform flaws are rated CVSS 10.0.

records.title: tcherber: Cyderes finds an access broker's Go toolkit with VPN clients for FortiGate and SonicWall that, once a tunnel is up, maps internal routes and sweeps Active Directory over LDAP; a credential file mixes default guest, admin and test logins with organisation-specific passwords (more than 500 FortiGate entries) and connection logs show root-level tunnels into multiple victims in May and June 2026
records.headline: Cyderes: 'tcherber' VPN toolkit for FortiGate and SonicWall, credential file mixing default and real logins, LDAP sweep
records.summary: Cyderes' Howler Cell recovered a Go toolkit that wraps OpenConnect for FortiGate and NetExtender for SonicWall, a credential file of more than 500 FortiGate entries mixing default guest, admin and test logins with organisation-specific passwords, and VPN connection logs showing sustained root-level tunnels into multiple victim environments in May and June 2026. Once the tunnel is up the orchestrator maps internal routes and enumerates Active Directory over LDAP, while port scanning, SMB reconnaissance and credential validation are manual tools. Cyderes assesses a Russian-speaking initial access broker and malware-as-a-service seller and names no victim, vulnerability or firmware version.
actions: Audit every FortiGate and SonicWall VPN gateway for VPN accounts with default or guessed passwords (guest, admin, test) or passwords that appear in credential dumps, reset or remove them, and search VPN logs since May 2026 for logins by such accounts that are followed by a broad LDAP enumeration from the VPN address pool, because Cyderes found a broker's toolkit and logs showing root-level tunnels into multiple victims.

records.title: CyberPower PowerPanel Business as a SYSTEM script channel on a domain controller: Symantec traces ntds.dit extraction with ntdsutil ifm and esentutl /vss and a side-loaded implant to scripts that the UPS-management service ppbed.exe runs as SYSTEM; Symantec does not say how the console was reached and no actor is named
records.headline: Symantec: attacker ran SYSTEM commands on a domain controller through CyberPower PowerPanel Business, then took ntds.dit
records.summary: Symantec analysed an intrusion in which the attacker used CyberPower PowerPanel Business, UPS-management software, as an execution channel on a Windows domain controller: scripts placed in the product's extcmd folder run through the ppbed.exe service as SYSTEM, and the operator iterated scripts until ntds.dit was exported with ntdsutil ifm and esentutl /vss, then side-loaded an implant. Symantec does not say how the attacker reached the console (public advisories or stolen administrator credentials could give that access) and names no actor.
actions: On every host that runs CyberPower PowerPanel Business, domain controllers first, compare the extcmd and temp\\profile\\extcmd folders with the product defaults and compare the extcmd folders and the console's event-to-command assignments with what administrators configured and treat unknown scripts as hostile; where the techniques Symantec lists are found (ntdsutil or esentutl on a domain controller, scripts staged under extcmd that no administrator configured, a side-loaded implant), assume Active Directory credentials are exposed and plan a krbtgt reset and wider credential rotation, because Symantec saw this channel used to export ntds.dit from a domain controller.

records.title: CVE-2026-19707, Airlock Gateway 8.5.0 to 8.5.2 and 8.6.0: attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response overflows a buffer in the Smart Form Protection feature and can cause denial of service or code execution on the gateway; fixed in 8.5.3 and 8.6.1, no exploitation reported (CVSS 4.0 9.5)
records.headline: Airlock Gateway: Smart Form Protection buffer overflow can crash or take over the gateway; update to 8.5.3 or 8.6.1
records.summary: Airlock (Ergon) published CVE-2026-19707 on 2026-11-18: attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response can overflow a buffer in the Smart Form Protection feature of Airlock Gateway 8.5.0 to 8.5.2 and 8.6.0, possibly causing denial of service or remote code execution against the gateway, when the feature is enabled on a mapping whose backend returns certain multi-byte HTML character references (CVSS 4.0 9.5, high attack complexity). The fix is in 8.5.3 and 8.6.1, no source reports exploitation, and Airlock says a compromised gateway could also affect the protection of the other backends behind it.
actions: Move every Airlock Gateway running 8.5.0 through 8.5.2 to 8.5.3 and every one running 8.6.0 to 8.6.1, starting with gateways that have Smart Form Protection enabled on a mapping whose backend serves user-supplied HTML, because Airlock says one backend response can crash or take over the gateway that protects every backend behind it.

records.title: CVE-2026-131914, Idunno.AntiCsrf 0.9.1 and earlier, a defunct anti-CSRF module for ASP.NET WebForms: one unauthenticated POST with a crafted CSRF form field is deserialized without validation and runs code in the IIS worker process; Mandiant observed exploitation in the wild and no patch exists, so the module has to be removed (CVSS 4.0 9.3)
records.headline: Idunno.AntiCsrf (ASP.NET WebForms) unauthenticated deserialization RCE exploited, no patch: remove the module
records.summary: Mandiant published CVE-2026-131914 on 2026-11-18 for Idunno.AntiCsrf, an open-source anti-CSRF HTTP module for ASP.NET WebForms last released in December 2008: any anonymously reachable page that does not opt out passes a crafted CSRF form field to an unvalidated deserializer, so one POST runs code in the IIS worker process (CVSS 4.0 9.3). Mandiant states that exploitation in the wild has been observed, names no actor, and says the project has no active maintainer or official patch, so the fix is to remove the module, and Mandiant adds that environments with evidence of exploitation should rotate the secrets held in the web configuration and inspect the web root.
actions: Search every ASP.NET WebForms application's Web.config and bin directory for Idunno.AntiCsrf by name, not by file hash because recompiled copies keep the flaw, and remove the module and its DLL, replacing it with a supported anti-forgery mechanism; on any server with evidence of exploitation, such as IIS requests to .aspx pages that returned 302 or 500 with unusually large request sizes, rotate the machineKey, encryption keys and database credentials in Web.config and applicationHost.config, because Mandiant observed exploitation and no patch exists.

records.title: CVE-2026-90817, REDCap 13.3.0 up to 16.0.48 LTS, 17.3.9 LTS and 17.4.3 Standard: an unauthenticated chain from a public survey request through the Data Import controller to code execution on the server, exploited as of 2026-10-07 for cryptocurrency mining and listed by CISA; fixed in 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS and 17.4.4 Standard (CVSS 3.1 9.8)
records.headline: REDCap unauthenticated survey-to-RCE chain exploited and on CISA KEV; upgrade to 16.0.49, 17.3.10 or 17.4.4
records.summary: Securifera described CVE-2026-90817 on 2026-09-27, a five-step chain in Vanderbilt's REDCap research-data platform that turns a request to a public survey into code execution on the server without authentication, given a valid public survey hash (CVSS 3.1 9.8). Unit 42 reported it exploited on 2026-10-07 to install Monero miners behind a transient web shell, with cron, SSH-key and shell-profile persistence, and CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-18. The fixed builds are 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS and 17.4.4 Standard.
actions: Upgrade every REDCap server to 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS or 17.4.4 Standard and, on any server that was internet-reachable on an older build, check for transient Blade-template files under the web temp cache, crontabs, the authorized_keys of every account, ~/.profile and Monero miner processes, treating a hit as a server compromise, because Unit 42 saw the chain used for mining with persistence that an upgrade does not remove.

records.summary: HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05162 of 2026-10-22 fixes 76 CVEs (72 in its first release, four added and one id replaced in revision 2 of 2026-11-17) in AOS-8 and AOS-10 for Mobility Conductors, Controllers, Gateways and access points, 33 of them at CVSS 3.1 9.0 or higher and 19 of those reachable over the network without authentication (eight at 10.0). records.title: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, PHP2Shell in management servers and storage: Trend Micro released critical patches for Apex Central and Apex One server on 2026-11-11, Mobile Security for Enterprise on 2026-11-17 and Deep Discovery Analyzer by 2026-11-18, Quest KACE SMA and SDA have fixes and should block ports 80, 443 and 52230 until patched, and NetApp ONTAP 9 is affected by CVE-2026-109618 only, inside the PHP jail
records.headline: PHP2Shell: Trend Micro Apex, Mobile Security and Analyzer patches out, Analyzer 7.5 gets none; Quest KACE, NetApp fixed
records.summary: Trend Micro posted Critical Patch build 7351 for Apex Central and build 20113 for Apex One Service Pack 1 on 2026-11-11, each upgrading PHP to 8.2.35 (the Apex One readme does not name the flaw), and its advisory, updated 2026-11-18, names both patches and lists critical patches 1020 for Deep Discovery Analyzer 7.7 and 1082 for 7.6 (none for 7.5, upgrade to 7.6) and for Deep Discovery Inspector and Email Inspector, while its Download Center carries a Mobile Security for Enterprise 9.8 SP5 patch dated 2026-11-17 that the advisory row has not caught up with; Quest says all KACE SMA and SDA versions are affected, with SMA 15.0 CU5 and 15.1 CU2 and the SDA 9.3 hotfix out and advice to block ports 80, 443 and 52230 until applied; and NetApp's advisory lists ONTAP 9 as affected only by CVE-2026-109618, with attacker access as the www user restricted to the PHP jail and hotfix builds from 9.12.1P20HF1 to 9.19.1P4. NetApp says it is aware of public discussion of the vulnerability and none of the three vendors reports an exploited case on its page, although CISA lists both flaws as exploited.
actions: Install Trend Micro's Apex Central Critical Patch build 7351 and Apex One Service Pack 1 Critical Patch build 20113 (both released 2026-11-11; the Apex One readme updates PHP to 8.2.35 without naming the flaw) on every server now and keep their consoles on administrator networks until done; install Mobile Security for Enterprise 9.8 SP5 Critical Patch 10 (build 3461) and the Deep Discovery Analyzer critical patch for the installed version (1020 on 7.7, 1082 on 7.6; 7.5 gets none, so upgrade to 7.6 first); install the critical patches the table lists for Deep Discovery Inspector and Email Inspector.
Install KACE SMA 15.0 CU5 or 15.1 CU2 and the SDA 9.3 hotfix 9.3.313 (9.3.312 where already installed), and until then block inbound ports 80, 443 and 52230 to every appliance, as Quest advises.

records.title: CVE-2026-90436, Atlassian Confluence Data Center 1.x to 9.x: remote code execution through the bundled Apache Axis behind the Remote API (XML-RPC and SOAP) when that API is enabled; fixed in 9.2.28, Confluence 10 not affected (CVSS 4.0 9.3)
records.headline: Confluence Data Center: Axis RCE (Remote API on) now exploited in N-able N-central; update to 9.2.28 or disable it
records.summary: Atlassian's advisory of 2026-11-09 says Apache Axis, which Confluence uses for its XML-RPC and SOAP APIs, has a critical remote-code-execution flaw (CVE-2026-90436, CVSS 4.0 9.3, no privileges or user interaction), exploitable in Confluence Data Center 1.x to 9.x only when the Remote API setting is enabled, which it is not by default for new installations. The fix is 9.2.28; the workaround is to clear the Remote API checkbox without a restart; Atlassian cannot confirm whether instances were affected and asks teams to check them; no source reports exploitation of Confluence, but the same flaw is exploited against N-able N-central servers that embed Axis.
actions: On every Confluence Data Center instance, open General Configuration, Further Configuration and clear the Remote API (XML-RPC & SOAP) checkbox now (no restart), confirm the soap-axis1 confluenceservice-v2 servlet path answers HTTP 403, and upgrade to 9.2.28, because Atlassian cannot confirm whether instances were affected and asks teams to check them for compromise.

records.headline: C3RB3R hits Synology NAS; CISA lists CVE-2024-10441 as exploited, 360 names the September pair; update DSM
records.summary: Synology said on 2026-10-29 that threat actors are exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to encrypt and extort devices on outdated DSM, naming no CVE and pointing to Synology-SA-24:20, while the Chinese vendor 360 identifies the ransomware as C3RB3R, a Cerber variant, and says it got in through CVE-2026-13684 and CVE-2026-13639, the two unauthenticated CVSS 9.8 flaws of Synology-SA-26:13 (fixed in DSM 7.4-90075, 7.3.2-86009-4, 7.2.2-72806-9 and 7.2.1-69057-12, with no mitigation). CISA added CVE-2024-10441, the lead flaw of SA-24:20, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-18, which supports Synology's pointer, while no source corroborates 360's naming of the two September flaws; a DSM that is current on both advisories is out of scope on either.
actions: Update every Synology DSM to the fixed build of its branch now (7.4-90075, 7.3.2-86009-4, 7.2.2-72806-9 or 7.2.1-69057-12, and 7.2-64570-4, 7.1.1-42962-7 or 6.2.4-25556-8 on the branches for which SA-26:13 names no fix; on DSM 7.1, 7.2 and 6.2 those builds close only the SA-24:20 flaws, so also move to a branch with an SA-26:13 fix), taking the management interface of any NAS that is reachable from the internet offline first, because Synology confirms ransomware is exploiting outdated DSM, CISA lists CVE-2024-10441 as exploited and Synology lists no mitigation for the September flaws.
On every NAS that was reachable from the internet on an older build, look in its shares for files renamed to .L0CK3D and for read-me3.txt notes, and isolate any hit.

records.title: CVE-2026-119618, Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 to 2.4.70: a race in mod_http2 assign_headers() corrupts heap memory and leads to remote code execution on servers with HTTP/2 enabled; fixed in 2.4.71, Red Hat calls it unauthenticated and claims public exploit research, Axis OS version 6.50.5.10 and higher is affected with no fixed release yet, no exploitation reported
records.headline: Apache httpd mod_http2 RCE: update to 2.4.71 or drop h2/h2c; Axis OS affected, no fix; Debian, Ubuntu, Red Hat fixed
records.summary: The Apache HTTP Server project released 2.4.71 on 2026-11-11 to fix CVE-2026-119618, a race in mod_http2 that it rates critical and says can lead to remote code execution in versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70; Red Hat adds that it is unauthenticated, affects only servers with HTTP/2 enabled through the Protocols directive, and that public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit, while no source reports exploitation. Red Hat has fixed RHEL 9 and 10, Debian bookworm and trixie, Alpine and SUSE Linux Enterprise 15 SP7 ship 2.4.71 packages, Ubuntu has shipped backported fixes, while a researcher's public test reproduces crashes on 2.4.70 and, per Wordfence, does not show code execution. Axis says AXIS OS version 6.50.5.10 and higher is affected, has no fixed release yet and gives a workaround that turns off HTTP/2 on the device.
actions: On every internet-facing Apache HTTP Server that loads mod_http2, update to 2.4.71 or to your distribution's fixed package (Debian bookworm 2.4.71-1~deb12u1, trixie 2.4.71-1~deb13u1 or forky and sid 2.4.71-1, Ubuntu per USN-9090-1, Alpine 2.4.71-r0, RHEL 9 mod_http2 2.0.26-7.el9_9.1, RHEL 10 mod_http2 2.0.29-5.el10_3.1) and restart it; update SUSE Linux Enterprise 15 SP7 to apache2 2.4.71-150700.4.30.1; where no fixed package exists yet, as on the SUSE products still in progress, remove h2 and h2c from the Protocols directive until one does, because Red Hat reports an unauthenticated code-execution path and a public exploit, though it rates its RHEL 9 and 10 packages Important rather than Critical for their harder exploitation.

On every Axis network device on AXIS OS version 6.50.5.10 or higher, set System.HTTP2.AllowH2 and System.HTTP2.AllowH2c to no through param.cgi now (Axis Device Manager mass-deploys it) and install the service release when Axis ships it, then revert the settings, because Axis says an unauthenticated attacker could gain administrator access and has released no fixed AXIS OS.

records.title: TYPO3 core security releases of 2026-11-17 (ten advisories): a low-privileged backend user can write a file into the web root and re-enable the unauthenticated installer, which creates an administrator and leads to code execution (SA-026, SA-027 Critical), and TYPO3 states that a Form Framework flaw (SA-029) is actively exploited; fixed in 14.3.12, 13.4.40, 12.4.52 ELTS, 11.5.57 ELTS and 10.4.63 ELTS
records.headline: TYPO3: backend user to installer to admin and RCE (SA-027 Critical); Form Framework flaw SA-029 exploited; update now
records.summary: TYPO3 published ten core advisories on 2026-11-17 for 10.0.0 to 14.3.11, fixed in 14.3.12 LTS, 13.4.40 LTS, 12.4.52 ELTS, 11.5.57 ELTS and 10.4.63 ELTS. The one rated Critical (SA-027) lets a file named FIRST_INSTALL placed in the web root re-enable the installer without authentication, which creates an administrator and leads to remote code execution, and SA-026 lets any low-privileged backend user create such a file. TYPO3 states that SA-029, a Medium information disclosure in the Form Framework that can become cross-site scripting through uploaded HTML, is known to be actively exploited, naming no actor or victim.
actions: Update every TYPO3 instance to 14.3.12, 13.4.40, 12.4.52 ELTS, 11.5.57 ELTS or 10.4.63 ELTS now, and on 14.x configure HTTP/allowed_hosts/dashboard_rss; until then check the public web root and the project root for unexpected files whose name starts with FIRST_INSTALL and the backend for administrator or system maintainer accounts nobody created, because a low-privileged backend user can re-enable the installer and TYPO3 states that one flaw in the same release is actively exploited.

records.title: Barracuda's own account of a 44-hour intrusion into its cloud: a key given to an AI vendor and never retired, found in that vendor's compromised development environment, led an intruder across about ten cloud accounts to Kubernetes; notified Managed XDR customers must recreate their integration credentials
records.headline: Barracuda: an unretired vendor cloud key led an ARTEX-consistent intruder across ten accounts in 44 hours
records.summary: Barracuda says an attacker used a valid cloud access key that it had issued to an AI-sector vendor for a past project and never retired, between 2026-11-01 04:33 and 2026-11-02 23:31 UTC, reading stored secrets and moving through about ten cloud accounts, a data analytics system, a source-code token and Kubernetes clusters. One system reached stores the credentials Barracuda Managed XDR uses to collect data from customers' connected systems; Barracuda found no direct evidence they were accessed, treated them as exposed and asked the customers it notified to revoke and recreate them. Barracuda says the activity is consistent with ARTEX, an AI-driven penetration-testing framework, and that this shows how the attacker worked, not who it was.
actions: If Barracuda notified you that your Managed XDR Cloud or Monitored Endpoint integration credentials may be affected, revoke and recreate each integration credential and review activity in the connected systems (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, endpoint security platforms and others) since 2026-11-01; Barracuda says an organisation it did not notify needs no action.

records.title: COLD RELIC: Mandiant shows the FSB-linked group reusing data stolen from one US organisation as the impersonation pretext for the next, then holding cloud tenants through MFA push fatigue and enrolled passkeys, backup codes and MFA devices that survive password and session resets
records.headline: Mandiant: COLD RELIC turns one cloud compromise into the pretext for the next; enrolled passkeys outlive password resets
records.summary: Mandiant reports that COLD RELIC, the name Google Threat Intelligence Group now uses for the group formerly tracked as COLDRIVER and UNC4057 (Star Blizzard), reused the staff directory and identities stolen from one US organisation in late 2025 to impersonate a contact when approaching a second in 2026. In the late-2025 case it took over a Super Admin account through push-notification fatigue, kept access with enrolled passkeys, MFA backup codes and rogue MFA devices that survived password and session resets, and exported the whole tenant; in 2026 it phished Entra ID credentials and registered a new MFA device to download one user's drive. GTIG names government officials, defense contractors and NGOs in Europe and North America as targets and says new phishing operations continued into November 2026.
actions: In every Google Workspace and Entra ID tenant you run, search the administrator and sign-in logs for passkey, backup-code and MFA-device enrolments on privileged accounts and for tenant-wide Customer Takeout exports, because COLD RELIC's enrolled authenticators survived password and session resets.

records.title: CVE-2026-123488, Craft CMS 4.0.0 to 4.18.8 and 5.0.0 to 5.11.1: an unauthenticated SQL injection in front-end search lets a visitor become an administrator on MySQL and MariaDB; the Canadian Cyber Centre reports exploitation in the wild and 4.18.9 and 5.11.2 fix it (CVSS 4.0 9.3)
records.headline: Craft CMS unauthenticated SQL injection gives admin takeover; CCCS reports exploitation; update to 4.18.9 or 5.11.2
records.summary: CVE-2026-123488 is an unauthenticated SQL injection in the front-end search of Craft CMS 4.0.0 to 4.18.8 and 5.0.0 to 5.11.1 on MySQL and MariaDB that gives read and write access to the database, including setting the admin flag or overwriting password hashes. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security says open source reporting indicates exploitation in the wild and VulnCheck lists it in its own KEV database; no first-hand telemetry or CISA listing was found. Craft fixed it in 4.18.9 and 5.11.2 and offers a query-string block as a workaround.
actions: Update every Craft CMS 4 site to 4.18.9 and every Craft CMS 5 site to 5.11.2 now, and where that waits block front-end requests whose query string contains [attribute] or its encoded form %5Battribute%5D; on each MySQL or MariaDB site that was internet-facing on an older build, check the users table for an admin flag or password hash nobody changed and for administrator accounts you did not create, because the flaw writes to the database and updating does not undo it.

records.title: GTIG AI Threat Tracker, November 2026: an exposed exploit_agent framework automates patch diffing, exploit drafting and execution without a human, a suspected North Korean cluster plants a Claude Code startup download in internal repositories, and PRC-nexus actors stage and exfiltrate through an LLM platform's file hosting
records.headline: GTIG quarterly: exploit_agent automates n-day exploitation, suspected DPRK cluster abuses .claude/settings.json
records.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant's quarterly AI threat update of 2026-11-16 reports an exposed multi-agent framework, exploit_agent, that compares code before and after patch announcements, drafts exploits and runs them with no human in the loop, the first such full automation GTIG has identified. It also reports a suspected MIDNIGHT NEPTUNE (North Korea) cluster that modified .claude/settings.json in victims' internal repositories so that Claude Code downloads the SOMBERMEME backdoor at startup, and PRC-nexus actors using an LLM platform's file-hosting backend for staging and exfiltration.

records.title: TGR-STA-0049: Unit 42 describes the PerfectPioneer and KUKURAT implants, which use HTTP/3 over QUIC for command and control against government networks entered through unpatched Exchange servers, then spread through domain logon scripts and grant FullAccess on every mailbox
records.headline: Unit 42: TGR-STA-0049 uses QUIC C2, logon-script spread and Exchange FullAccess loops against governments
records.summary: Unit 42 reports that TGR-STA-0049 (also tracked as REF7707, Earth Alux and Ink Dragon) has attacked Southeast Asian government entities since at least July 2025, entering through unpatched Exchange and web servers, and says the group's targeting also includes governments in South America and Europe. Its new PerfectPioneer and KUKURAT implants use HTTP/3 over QUIC as the main command channel in most variants, the operators spread KUKURAT through domain logon scripts after taking a domain controller, and on Exchange they grant a compromised account FullAccess on every mailbox.

records.headline: ARTEX in AWS: CloudWatch log searches for secrets, Cognito self-sign-up for credentials; hunt CloudTrail for both
records.summary: Datadog Security Labs reports that in October 2026 operators of the ARTEX agentic penetration-testing framework worked against several AWS environments with a focus on financial data: sessions opened with anonymous S3 reads, a stolen long-term IAM key drove CloudWatch Logs FilterLogEvents searches for company names, passwords and access keys, and where no key was held the agent self-registered in a public Cognito user pool and traded the tokens for AWS credentials. records.title: CVE-2026-98432, Linux kernel IPv4 TCP: a use-after-free in connection setup, present since 4.4, has an Anthropic-built remote root exploit against MPTCP listeners that CloudLinux could not reproduce; Citrix XenServer, XCP-ng, MikroTik, Red Hat, Debian, CIQ, Amazon Linux, Ubuntu's generic kernels for 22.04 to 26.10 and Sophos have fixes, Ubuntu 20.04 and older and some HWE, FIPS, NVIDIA and Azure variant kernels are in progress and WatchGuard and Fortinet have none for their products (CVSS 9.8)
records.headline: Linux TCP use-after-free: Sophos hotfix and Ubuntu generic kernels out; WatchGuard, Fortinet have no fixed build
records.summary: The Linux kernel CVE team published CVE-2026-98432 on 2026-10-15, a use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP connection setup path that dates to Linux 4.4 and is reached by a SYN packet carrying IP options; the CNA scores it CVSS 9.8. Anthropic reports that Claude wrote an exploit giving a remote, unauthenticated attacker root on servers with a multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener, which CloudLinux's kernel team could not reproduce; the Go team says the bug is not specific to MPTCP and Akamai that disabling MPTCP does not prevent exploitation, and no source reports attacks. Citrix rates its XenServer 8.4 and 9 bulletin Critical and names fixes for Workload Balancing and Conversion Manager, XCP-ng released a kernel fix, MikroTik's RouterOS 7.25.1 and 7.24.6 list the CVE, Red Hat, Debian, CIQ and Amazon Linux kernels are fixed, Ubuntu has fixed its generic kernels for 22.04 to 26.10 while 20.04 and older and some HWE, FIPS, NVIDIA and Azure variant kernels were still in progress on 2026-11-10, and Sophos has shipped a Firewall hotfix and SD-RED firmware, while WatchGuard (Fireware OS, AP, Dimension) and Fortinet list their products as unresolved or under investigation without a fixed build, Fortinet offering an IPS virtual patch.
actions: On every internet-facing Linux server and every XenServer or XCP-ng host with its Workload Balancing and Conversion Manager appliances, install the vendor's fixed kernel or firmware and reboot, then confirm the running version.

On Veeam estates, run Veeam Updater on the appliances, install the private fix for the Linux helper appliances of Windows-based Backup & Replication and of Recovery Orchestrator 13.1, redeploy virtual labs and helper appliances that stay deployed and replace recovery media made before the update.

On hosts that cannot reboot yet, drop IPv4 TCP packets that carry IP options ahead of the TCP stack as CIQ, AWS and Vates describe, after testing on one non-production host because it also drops legitimate option-bearing traffic; disabling MPTCP alone does not close the path.

records.headline: AhsayCBS chain exploited and in CISA KEV: standard releases v9.17.0 and v10.3.6 list a patchset for both flaws
records.summary: Huntress observed from 2026-10-07 23:20 UTC attackers chaining two AhsayCBS flaws, CVE-2026-105133 (authentication bypass) and CVE-2026-105134 (code execution as SYSTEM through the Replication Receiver API), against internet-exposed servers of the backup management console that managed service providers and system integrators mainly use, dropping JSP webshells and an XMRig cryptominer; Bitdefender MDR investigated three intrusions through the same chain, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14. Ahsay now says its earlier patches v9.15.2.59 and v10.3.4.0 did not fully address the flaws, so servers on them are still exposed; v9.17.0 of 2026-11-12, a standard release, carries Ahsay's patchset for both CVEs and turns remote API access and the JSP engine off by default, the v10 standard release v10.3.6 of 2026-11-02 lists the same patchset, the latest partner hotfixes v9.15.2.78 and v10.3.4.55 of 2026-10-27 remain an option, and a server that was reachable before the fix needs a compromise check.
actions: Find every AhsayCBS server your organisation or your managed-service suppliers run, including those on v10.3.4.0 or v9.15.2.59, and install v9.17.0 on v9 or v10.3.6 (current build v10.3.6.14) on v10, or the latest partner hotfix (v9.15.2.78 for v7 to v9, v10.3.4.55 for v10) and reboot after it, now; until then keep the management web interface behind a VPN or an allowlist of trusted addresses.

Compromise-check every AhsayCBS server that was internet-reachable since 2026-10-04, re-image any host with a finding from a trusted backup and rotate the credentials stored on or reachable from it, other backup software on the same network included, because the fix does not remove a webshell or persistence that is already there.

records.summary: VulnCheck, as CNA, published 14 CVEs on 2026-11-12 for XWEB EVO, the end-of-service Copeland and Dixell web supervisor for refrigeration and cold-chain equipment, seven of them scored CVSS 4.0 9.2 to 9.3: unauthenticated command injection that runs as root, a hard-coded Administrator password, and Administrator and root passwords computed from the device MAC address and date. records.title: The Gentlemen affiliate: an SSL-VPN account without MFA, a Windows Server 2003 host and a dormant local administrator gave Domain Admin in under an hour; the GPO locker most likely lost a replication race, so antivirus was disabled estate-wide but only one host was encrypted (Ransom-ISAC)
records.headline: Ransom-ISAC: Gentlemen affiliate, VPN without MFA to Domain Admin in an hour; GPO locker likely lost a replication race
records.summary: Ransom-ISAC's incident-response report describes an early-August 2026 intrusion by a Gentlemen ransomware affiliate that began with an SSL-VPN account without MFA and reached Domain Admin in under an hour, most likely with credentials taken from an end-of-life Windows Server 2003 host that a dormant local administrator account opened, then used a Rust credential harvester and the EtherRAT implant. The locker's GPO disabled antivirus across the estate but the task that runs it most likely never reached clients because of a replication race, so the locker ran on one host; the report names the telemetry at each step. Single source, no victim named.

records.title: ScreenConnect: Huntress finds 2,223 fake guest sessions named after crypto exchanges on 118 self-hosted servers, enrolled from 2026-11-03 and, in its leading hypothesis, bait for technicians whose clients predate 26.6.5; it saw no malicious use and no overlap with SCKit
records.headline: Huntress: 2,223 crypto-named fake sessions sit on 118 ScreenConnect servers, likely bait for unpatched technicians
records.summary: Huntress counted 2,223 unauthorized guest sessions on 118 self-hosted ScreenConnect servers at 109 MSP and organisation accounts, enrolled between 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-13 and named after crypto exchanges; on the 29 servers with complete history an operator revisited every 151 seconds to keep them online. Huntress's leading hypothesis, which it has not observed, is that they are bait for a technician with a client older than 26.6.5 to connect, so that CVE-2026-84869 runs a file on the technician's workstation; it saw no malicious activity from the sessions and found no overlap with the SCKit indicators.
actions: On every self-hosted ScreenConnect server your organisation or its IT providers run, list guest sessions with an exchange-and-role name or empty company or site fields, copy App_Data\\Session.db and its WAL file before deleting any, and where a technician connected to one from a client older than 26.6.5, inspect that workstation's ScreenConnect Temp and Startup folders and process history and treat text sent through the session as exposed credentials, because Huntress suspects the sessions are bait for the file-transfer flaw CVE-2026-84869.

records.title: Cursor marketplace: a tampered Claude Code extension (versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313) planted an SSH key, a reverse tunnel and persistence for about eleven hours on 2026-10-29; uninstalling it does not remove the persistence
records.headline: Cursor marketplace served a trojanised Claude Code extension for 11 hours; uninstalling leaves the SSH backdoor
records.summary: Between about 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29 the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace served a modified copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for macOS and Windows, that appends an attacker's SSH key to authorized_keys, tries to enable SSH and open a reverse tunnel, and installs persistence that outlives the extension; coding errors made the SSH step fail on most standard-user hosts, so Cursor says the attacker could not log in there. Cursor's report of 2026-11-13 says the chain began with an access key it had issued to its vendor Fireworks AI, exposed by Fireworks, which gave the attacker a storage bucket of coding-agent traces holding some unredacted credentials, and that a stolen credential from the exposed data let the attacker write the extension straight onto the marketplace cache; Cursor says this was not a vulnerability in Anthropic's product.
actions: On every developer endpoint that runs Cursor, check extension-install telemetry for Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 installed between 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29; where it is found, isolate the host, remove the unauthorized SSH key, the persistence and any running tunnel process, because uninstalling the extension removes none of them, and rotate every credential reachable from the host from a trusted system.

Ask the admin of every Cursor team your organisation uses whether Cursor's email listing exposed keys arrived, and rotate every key it lists, because Cursor says coding-agent traces from sessions outside Privacy Mode held unredacted credentials.

records.title: Kaspersky GERT BlackNevas case: credentials from systems outside the virtualisation layer reach both vCenter appliances, a remote-access agent and a VMware-lookalike tunnel service persist, vCenter Host Profile remediation switches SSH on across the ESXi hosts, backups are destroyed first and a wipe of the datastores detonates over ten days, with no vulnerability exploited
records.headline: Kaspersky: BlackNevas used vCenter Host Profiles to enable SSH on ESXi, destroyed backups first, then wiped datastores
records.summary: Kaspersky GERT describes a ten-day engagement in which an adversary, identified as BlackNevas from its ransom notes, used credentials taken from systems outside the virtualisation layer to reach both vCenter appliances, persisted on one with a remote-access agent and a tunnel installed as a VMware-lookalike systemd service, then used vCenter Host Profile remediation to switch SSH on across four ESXi hosts, destroyed the backup environment first and detonated a wiper-capable locker that took every virtual machine. Kaspersky states no initial access vector, victim sector or country, and no virtualisation-layer vulnerability was exploited.

records.headline: GitLab critical patch: a merge request can reach a Git heap overflow on Gitaly; update to 19.5.4, 19.4.6 or 19.3.8
records.summary: GitLab shipped an ad-hoc critical patch release on 2026-11-10 for CVE-2026-105437, a heap overflow in Git that, per GitLab, any user who can create a project and open a merge request reaches, and that can run commands as the git user with access to every repository on that Gitaly node. Git 2.56.1 and its backports fix the same flaw and five others, among them CVE-2026-111760, code execution when a malicious repository is cloned with --recurse-submodules; no source reports exploitation.
actions: Upgrade every self-managed GitLab to 19.5.4, 19.4.6 or 19.3.8 now (self-compiled installs rebuild the Git in Gitaly and the Git at git.bin_path, or move the distribution Git to 2.56.1 or later) and, where that waits, limit who can create projects and sign up, because a user who can open a merge request reaches the flaw and code execution gives access to every repository on the Gitaly node.

records.headline: Red Hat Quay: anonymous signing-key takeover and cross-tenant token theft; update to your branch's fixed release

Red Hat fixed both in Quay 3.9.28, 3.10.28, 3.12.24, 3.14.10, 3.15.9, 3.16.7, 3.17.7 and 3.18.3, lists Quay 5 and the mirror registry for Red Hat OpenShift 2 as affected with no fix, and NCSC Switzerland lists exploitation as unknown.
actions: Update every Red Hat Quay registry to its branch's fixed release (3.9.28, 3.10.28, 3.12.24, 3.14.10, 3.15.9, 3.16.7, 3.17.7 or 3.18.3) and, until then, restrict the /keys endpoint at the proxy or load balancer to trusted internal components; on any instance whose /keys endpoint untrusted clients could reach, review audit logs for service_key_rotate and service_key_delete events with a null expiration_date and remove unrecognised approved service keys, because deleting a rogue key is not durable before the fix and resetting passwords or regenerating robot tokens does not revoke it.

records.title: ScreenConnect: commands pushed through Run Command to at least 288 managed endpoints at 48 Huntress customers within 90 minutes on 2026-11-11 installed a rogue second client and the SCKit toolkit; Huntress links the activity to the RMM+ extension, whose versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 accepted a blank access key
records.headline: ScreenConnect SCKit: second wave hits on-prem; disable RMM+, update technician clients to 26.6.5+
records.summary: Huntress saw an operator use access to several cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels on 2026-11-11 to run Run Command as SYSTEM on groups of managed endpoints, installing an attacker-controlled second ScreenConnect client and the SCKit toolkit on at least 288 hosts at 48 organisations within 90 minutes; Sophos independently saw the same client deployments. Huntress later said the activity seems related to the third-party RMM+ extension, whose versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 accepted a blank access key; ConnectWise's CNA record CVE-2026-127063 (CVSS 4.0 9.3) says the extension uses a static API secret by default, names no fix and gives disabling as the mitigation, while a Huntress spokesperson says the panel-access vector is still unclear and Blackpoint calls the extensions' role unresolved. A second wave on 2026-11-13 hit 205 hosts at 41 organisations (Huntress) and appears to target on-premises instances with mitigations pending (Blackpoint); Microsoft describes a rogue client built to deliver a payload to the technician who connects, which ConnectWise says ScreenConnect clients 26.6.5 and later block.
actions: On every ScreenConnect instance your organisation or its IT providers run, disable the RMM+ extension immediately, verify it stays disabled and do not re-enable or reinstall it (on-premises instances by hand; ConnectWise removed it from cloud-hosted ones), review Run Command and Toolbox history and the instance audit logs for executions nobody started, including before 2026-11-11, and check managed endpoints for a second ScreenConnect client service; open no interactive session to a suspect host, use EDR live response or WinRM, because a session can trigger the toolkit to spread to the technician's workstation; update every technician host client to ScreenConnect 26.6.5 or later, because a cloud-console update does not update them.

records.title: Luna Moth returns to law firms that likely did not pay, with a token handoff: a video-call 'IT support' agent has the employee copy a Microsoft Graph access token out of Microsoft 365 Copilot through browser developer tools, then bulk-downloads files from the attacker's own server (ReliaQuest)
records.headline: ReliaQuest: Luna Moth has staff hand over a Graph token from Copilot on a video call; no sign-in event follows
records.summary: ReliaQuest reports that the data-extortion group Luna Moth (Silent Ransom Group) returned in October and early November to law firms it had extorted in May and August, using a technique it calls almost certainly new for the group: on a video call posing as IT support the attacker has the employee open Microsoft 365 Copilot, copy the Microsoft Graph access token out of the browser's developer tools and paste it to a text-sharing site, then replays it from its own server and downloads thousands of files in about an hour. The token was issued to the victim's compliant device, so no sign-in event is generated for the attacker's address; ReliaQuest is the only source and names no victim or country.

records.title: CyberStrikeAI turned on AWS: Elastic reads one server's 16 days across eight identities in four accounts, 56 user-data reads in 141 milliseconds, and why six detections each rated medium or low and only the source address tied them together
records.headline: Elastic: CyberStrikeAI against AWS, six medium or low alerts joined only by source IP; alert on user-data bursts
records.summary: Elastic Security Labs reports that between 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-16 one server running the open-source CyberStrikeAI platform used the credentials of eight AWS identities (five IAM users, three EC2 instance roles) across four accounts, reading secrets and EC2 user data and, in one case, issuing a Systems Manager command. Every step is a call a legitimate role makes daily, so six detection rules each fired at medium or low severity and only the shared source address showed they belonged to one intrusion; Elastic does not know how the credentials were obtained and names no victim.
